docs.text: XTS API XTS API (Xtreme Trading System API) is a complete trading framework that connects your application directly to brokers and stock exchanges — enabling market data, order management, portfolio services, and real-time updates. Secure authentication Place & manage orders Portfolio & holdings Real-time WebSocket Live market quotes Easy integration What is XTS API? XTS API acts as a bridge between your application and the stock exchange . It separates into two independent channels — Market Data (read-only feeds) and Interactive (two-way trading operations) — so network traffic never interferes with your orders. Market Data API Read-only market information Live market quotes & OHLC Historical price data Market depth (order book) Instrument search WebSocket quote streaming Interactive API Two-way trading operations User authentication & sessions Place / Modify / Cancel orders Holdings & positions Funds & margin Real-time order updates API Request Flow User Login → Authentication → Access Token → API Request → XTS Gateway → Broker / Exchange → Response REST vs WebSocket REST APIs Request → Response pattern Login & authentication Place / modify / cancel orders Fetch holdings & positions Check funds & margin WebSocket APIs Continuous real-time stream Live market quotes Order status updates Trade execution alerts Position P&L changes Welcome to RMoney APIs About RMoney RMoney is a technology-driven stock broking and investment platform that provides traders and investors with access to financial markets through modern trading applications, desktop platforms, and APIs. RMoney enables users to trade across multiple market segments including Equity, Futures & Options (F&O), Currency, and Commodities. Along with manual trading, RMoney also provides API-based trading infrastructure that allows developers and traders to build custom applications, automate trading strategies, and access market data programmatically. What are RMoney APIs? RMoney APIs are a collection of developer interfaces that allow applications to communicate directly with the RMoney trading ecosystem. Instead of placing orders manually, developers can use APIs to perform actions automatically. Retrieve live market prices Access historical market data Place buy and sell orders Track positions and holdings Monitor portfolios Receive real-time market updates Build algorithmic trading systems These APIs are based on the Symphony XTS framework and are designed for high-speed trading and market data access. Why Use RMoney APIs? RMoney APIs help developers and traders build powerful financial applications without needing to create trading infrastructure from scratch. Automated trading Real-time market access Fast order execution Portfolio management Custom trading dashboards Strategy automation Market analytics Trading bots Whether you are building a simple stock tracker or a complete algorithmic trading platform, RMoney APIs provide the building blocks required for development. API Categories RMoney APIs are divided into different categories based on functionality. Market Data APIs Access live and historical market information for stocks, derivatives, and more. Commonly used in charting applications, watchlists, screeners, and analytics platforms. Get real-time stock prices Access historical data Retrieve OHLC candles View market depth Search instruments Receive tick-by-tick updates Explore Market Data APIs → Trading APIs Place and manage orders directly through your application. The foundation of automated trading systems and trading platforms. Place orders Modify orders Cancel orders Check order status Track positions Manage portfolios Explore Trading APIs → Portfolio APIs Monitor investments and trading activity with detailed account information. Useful for portfolio management systems and investment dashboards. Holdings Positions Funds & margins Profit & Loss Account summary Explore Portfolio APIs → WebSocket APIs Receive real-time streaming data with persistent WebSocket connections. Ideal for low-latency trading applications. Live market ticks Real-time quotes Order updates Position updates Market depth updates Explore WebSocket APIs → Supported Market Segments RMoney APIs support multiple trading segments through a unified interface, allowing developers to manage different asset classes using a single API ecosystem. Equity Equity Intraday Futures Options Currency Commodities Technology & Integration RMoney APIs can be integrated with various technologies and programming languages, allowing developers to build applications using their preferred technology stack. Python Java C++ C# JavaScript .NET Excel Who Can Use RMoney APIs? RMoney APIs are designed for a wide range of users in the financial and technology space. 📈 Traders Automate strategies and execute trades faster than manual trading. 💻 Developers Build custom trading applications and financial tools. 🏢 FinTech Companies Integrate market data and trading capabilities into products. 🔬 Researchers Analyze historical data and develop quantitative models. 🤖 Algo Traders Automate complete trading workflows using APIs. Typical API Workflow A typical RMoney API workflow covers the full cycle from login to real-time updates, powering most trading and investment applications. User logs in Authentication token is generated Application requests market data User selects an instrument Order is placed Order status is monitored Positions and portfolio are updated Real-time updates via WebSocket streams Key Features Real-Time Market Data Historical Market Data Fast Order Execution Portfolio Tracking Multi-Segment Trading WebSocket Streaming Strategy Automation Order Management Instrument Search Risk Monitoring Algo Trading Support Developer-Friendly APIs Getting Started Follow these steps to start using RMoney APIs and build your first trading application. Open an RMoney trading account. Request API access from the RMoney team. Generate your API credentials from the dashboard. Authenticate your application using the Interactive API. Start accessing market data and trading services. Ready to Build? Once authenticated, you can build trading applications, analytics platforms, investment tools, and automated trading systems using the RMoney API ecosystem. Reference Manual 📘 The Complete Reference Manual: Symphony XTS API v2 & Python Client Library Welcome! This is a comprehensive, standalone guide designed for new users and programmers to master the Symphony XTS Front-End API (v2.0) and its official Python client library, xts-api-client. No prior experience with trading APIs is required. We explain everything from high-level architecture to low-level parameters, supplemented by visual diagrams and code examples. 1 High-Level Concepts & Mental Models What is XTS? Symphony XTS is a high-speed trading system interface. It sits between your custom software (trading bot, dashboard, or scanner) and the stock brokers/exchanges (like NSE, BSE, MCX). The Two-Channel Split (Dual Engine) To prevent network traffic jams, XTS separates commands into two entirely independent channels: Interactive API : Private and secure. Used to place trades, check cash balances, query open positions, and get instant notifications when your orders fill. Market Data API : Public and read-only. Used to fetch stock names, request historical candle data, and stream real-time price updates (LTP, bid/ask spreads). 2 Technical Vocabulary & Business Rules Before writing code, you must understand the terminology used in API parameters: A. Exchange Segments Tells XTS which market segment you are querying: NSECM (1): National Stock Exchange Cash Market (Buying actual shares of Reliance, TCS, etc.) NSEFO (2): National Stock Exchange Futures & Options (Trading Nifty options/futures) NSECD (3): National Stock Exchange Currency Derivatives (USD/INR trading) MCXFO (51): Multi Commodity Exchange Futures & Options (Gold, Silver, Crude Oil) BSECM (11) & BSEFO (12): Bombay Stock Exchange equivalents B. Product Types Tells the broker how to manage the trade margin and holding period: MIS (Margin Intraday Square-off): Closed automatically before market shuts. Offers high leverage. NRML (Normal): Used to hold futures & options contracts for multiple days. CNC (Cash and Carry): Used to buy actual stock shares for long-term investing. No leverage. C. Order Types MARKET: Buys/sells immediately at the best available current market price. LIMIT: Executes only at your specified price or better. STOPMARKET: Triggered when the market price hits a target trigger price, then executes as a Market order. STOPLIMIT: Triggered when the market price hits a target trigger price, then places a Limit order. D. Time In Force (Validity) DAY: The order is valid until the market closes today. IOC (Immediate or Cancel): The order must execute instantly, or any unfilled part is cancelled. FOK (Fill or Kill): The entire order must execute instantly in full, or the whole order is cancelled. 3 Library Architecture & File Structure Here is a map of the xts-api-client package, detailing what each file does: 4 REST API Reference: Authentication & Session Every action requires a session token. Here is the lifecycle of an XTS session: --- Authentication Endpoints Interactive Login: POST /interactive/user/session Interactive Logout: DELETE /interactive/user/session Market Data Login: POST /apimarketdata/auth/login Market Data Logout: DELETE /apimarketdata/auth/logout Python Authentication Code Example import asyncio from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect async def manage_session(): # 1. Initialize the clients interactive_client = XTSConnect( apiKey="your_interactive_key", secretKey="your_interactive_secret", source="WEBAPI", root="https://api.yourbroker.com" ) # 2. Login (This fetches and automatically saves the token to client.token) login_resp = await interactive_client.interactive_login() print("Interactive Logged In! Token:", interactive_client.token) print("User ID:", interactive_client.userID) # 3. Log out to clean up session logout_resp = await interactive_client.interactive_logout() print("Logged out successfully!") asyncio.run(manage_session()) 5 Interactive API (Trading Operations) The Interactive client manages your money, orders, and positions. A. Order Placement & The Order Lifecycle When you submit an order, it moves through a state machine inside the exchange: B. Order Parameters Deep Dive When calling place_order() , you must specify the following parameters: response = await client.place_order( exchangeSegment="NSECM", # "NSECM", "NSEFO", "MCXFO" exchangeInstrumentID=2885, # Numeric code for the stock (e.g. 2885 for RELIANCE) productType="MIS", # "MIS" (Intraday), "NRML" (F&O Carryover), "CNC" (Equity Delivery) orderType="LIMIT", # "MARKET", "LIMIT", "STOPMARKET", "STOPLIMIT" orderSide="BUY", # "BUY" or "SELL" timeInForce="DAY", # "DAY", "IOC" disclosedQuantity=0, # Quantity visible to public order book (0 hides nothing) orderQuantity=10, # Total quantity to buy/sell limitPrice=2450.50, # Price to execute (required if LIMIT or STOPLIMIT) stopPrice=0.0, # Trigger price (required if STOPMARKET or STOPLIMIT) orderUniqueIdentifier="my_bot_01" # Custom string tag to track this specific order ) C. Advanced Order Types (Cover & Bracket) 1. Cover Orders (CO) A Cover Order has a stop-loss order chained directly to it . It is highly leveraged and requires an entry transaction and a trigger price (the stop-loss activation level). 1. Entry Order (Market or Limit) If Filled ⟶ 2. Stop Loss triggerPrice (Active on Exchange) If price hits Trigger level ⟶ 3. Executed Exit (Market Order) Cover Order Parameters & Code: # Place a Cover Order: Buy Reliance at market, stop-loss trigger active at ₹2400 co_response = await client.place_cover_order( exchangeSegment="NSECM", exchangeInstrumentID=2885, orderSide="BUY", orderType="MARKET", orderQuantity=5, disclosedQuantity=0, limitPrice=0.0, # 0.0 because orderType is MARKET stopPrice=2400.0, # Stop Loss Trigger level orderUniqueIdentifier="co_trade_01" ) 2. Bracket Orders (BO) A Bracket Order surrounds your entry order with two bracket legs: a Take Profit Target and a Stop-Loss Protection. Both exit orders are sent to the exchange as a One-Cancels-the-Other (OCO) pair. Bracket Order Parameters & Code: # Place a Bracket Order: Buy Reliance at ₹2450. Sell at ₹2500 for profit (+50) or ₹2420 for loss (-30) bo_response = await client.place_bracketorder( exchangeSegment="NSECM", exchangeInstrumentID=2885, orderType="LIMIT", orderSide="BUY", disclosedQuantity=0, orderQuantity=10, limitPrice=2450.00, squarOff=50.0, # Profit target offset (added to entry price) stopLossPrice=30.0, # Stop-Loss protection offset (subtracted from entry price) trailingStoploss=0.0, # 0.0 means inactive. Set value to adjust SL up as price rises isProOrder=False, # Set True for proprietary trading accounts orderUniqueIdentifier="bo_trade_01" ) D. Spread & GTT Orders 1. Spread Orders Spread orders let you trade price differences between two stock options or futures contracts simultaneously (e.g. buying July Futures and selling August Futures). Place Spread: POST /interactive/orders/spread Modify Spread: PUT /interactive/orders/spread Cancel Spread: DELETE /interactive/orders/spread 2. GTT (Good-Till-Triggered) Orders GTT orders remain active in the system for weeks or months until a target trigger price is hit. Once hit, it launches a standard order. Place GTT: POST /interactive/orders/gtt GTT Order Book: GET /interactive/orders/gtt/orderbook Cancel GTT: DELETE /interactive/orders/gtt E. Portfolio Management & Positions Once you have active trades, you query your balances and positions: async def query_portfolio(client): # 1. Available margin and cash balance balance = await client.get_balance() available_cash = balance['result']['BalanceList'][0]['limitObject']['RMSSubLimits']['cashAvailable'] print(f"Available Cash: ₹{available_cash}") # 2. Holdings (Long-term stocks held in your demat account) holdings = await client.get_holding() print("Holdings List:", holdings['result']) # 3. Daywise positions (Today's trading activity) day_pos = await client.get_position_daywise() # 4. Netwise positions (Current active net open positions) net_pos = await client.get_position_netwise() for pos in net_pos['result']: print(f"Instrument: {pos['ExchangeInstrumentID']} | Open Qty: {pos['NetQty']} | MTM PnL: ₹{pos['MTM']}") # 5. Convert Position (e.g., convert Intraday 'MIS' to Delivery 'CNC') await client.convert_position( exchangeSegment="NSECM", exchangeInstrumentID=2885, targetQty=5, isDayWise=True, oldProductType="MIS", newProductType="CNC" ) F. Margin Calculator APIs You can request how much cash margin is required to place or modify orders before actually sending them: Regular Margin: POST /interactive/margin/regular Cover Margin: POST /interactive/margin/cover Bracket Margin: POST /interactive/margin/bracket --- 6 Market Data API (Feeds & Queries) The Market Data client fetches historical chart candles, instrument identifiers, and subscriptions. async def query_market_data(market_client): # 1. Search for a security by trading symbol search_resp = await market_client.search_by_scriptname("TATAMOTORS") instrument_id = search_resp['result'][0]['ExchangeInstrumentID'] print(f"TATA Motors Instrument ID: {instrument_id}") # 2. Query Expiry Dates for Options/Futures contracts expiries = await market_client.get_expiry_date( exchangeSegment=2, # NSEFO series="OPTIDX", # Index Option symbol="NIFTY" ) print("Nifty Option Expiries:", expiries['result']) # 3. Retrieve Historical Chart Candles (OHLC) candles = await market_client.get_ohlc( exchangeSegment=1, # NSECM exchangeInstrumentID=22, # NIFTY Index startTime="Jun 01 2026 091500", # MMM DD YYYY HHMMSS endTime="Jun 15 2026 153000", compressionValue=5 # 5-minute intervals ) print("Raw Candle Data:", candles['result']['dataReponse'][:200]) 7 Real-time Socket Streaming (WebSockets via Socket.IO) WebSockets establish a constant, open channel of communication. Data flows automatically without your software having to ask for it. Step 1: Connection URL Breakdown The library connects to the socket using a specific query string: Interactive Socket: {root_url}/?token={token}&userID={userID}&apiType=INTERACTIVE Market Data Socket: {root_url}/?token={token}&userID={userID}&publishFormat=JSON&broadcastMode=Full Step 2: The Event Code Map The Market Data socket streams message packets prefixed with numeric event codes : Step 3: Complete WebSocket Listener Implementation To catch these events, you subclass MarketDataSocketClient (for prices) or InteractiveSocketClient (for trading updates) and assign it to the socket managers: import asyncio from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect from xts_api_client.market_data_socket import MDSocket_io from xts_api_client.market_data_socket_client import MarketDataSocketClient # 1. Create your listener implementation class RealTimePriceFeed(MarketDataSocketClient): async def on_connect(self): print(" Connected to live price feeds!") async def on_disconnect(self): print(" Socket disconnected!") async def on_error(self, data): print(" Error from Socket:", data) # Event 1512: LTP Ticks async def on_event_last_traded_price_full(self, data): print(f"Price Tick -> ID: {data['ExchangeInstrumentID']} | Price: ₹{data['LastTradedPrice']}") # Event 1501: Bid/Ask Depth Ticks async def on_event_touchline_full(self, data): print(f"Spread -> Bid: {data['BidInfo']['Price']} | Ask: {data['AskInfo']['Price']}") # 2. Main initialization script async def stream_prices(): # Login HTTP first client = XTSConnect( apiKey="your_market_key", secretKey="your_market_secret", source="WEBAPI", root="https://api.yourbroker.com" ) await client.marketdata_login() # Assign socket listener listener = RealTimePriceFeed() socket_client = MDSocket_io( token=client.token, userID=client.userID, root_url=client.root, marketdatasocketclient=listener ) # Establish connection await socket_client.connect() # Subscribe to Reliance (2885) and Nifty (22) instruments = [ {"exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 2885}, {"exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 22} ] await client.send_subscription(Instruments=instruments, xtsMessageCode=1512) # Keep the program running to see ticks stream await asyncio.sleep(20) # Clean up await socket_client.disconnect() await client.marketdata_logout() if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(stream_prices()) 8 Mark-To-Market (MTM) PnL Calculations Symphony calculates your unrealized profit or loss (PnL) in real-time. Here is how the math works: Total PnL = Realized PnL + Unrealized PnL Realized PnL Realized PnL is locked in when you complete a trade loop (Buy and Sell the same contract). Realized PnL = (Sell Price − Buy Price) × Traded Quantity Unrealized PnL Unrealized PnL fluctuates as the market price moves. It is calculated on open positions: For Long Positions (Open Quantity > 0): Unrealized PnL = (Current LTP − Average Buy Price) × Open Quantity For Short Positions (Open Quantity < 0): Unrealized PnL = (Average Sell Price − Current LTP) × Open Quantity (Absolute) 9 Helper Library Utilities The client library includes xts_api_client.helper.helper to parse and manage incoming data structures automatically. 1. Master List Parser (Pandas DataFrame) Symphony sends large stock master files as pipeline-separated string streams. The helper converts them to clean Pandas dataframes: from xts_api_client.helper.helper import cm_master_string_to_df, fo_master_string_to_df # Assume 'raw_csv_response' is retrieved from get_master() call df_equities = cm_master_string_to_df(raw_csv_response) # You can now run pandas queries print(df_equities[df_equities['Name'] == 'RELIANCE']) 2. MS-DOS Time Zone Converter Exchange times are given as seconds elapsed since the MS-DOS Epoch (1980-01-01). The helper translates this to standard Unix nanoseconds: from xts_api_client.helper.helper import dostime_secomds_to_unixtime unix_nanoseconds = dostime_secomds_to_unixtime(1464972900) print("Standard Unix timestamp:", unix_nanoseconds) 3. Account-Wide Squareoff Helper The helper provides a routine to retrieve all your open positions and instantly exit them at market price to protect capital in emergencies: from xts_api_client.helper.helper import async_squareoff_all_positions_ # Retrieve all positions and close them out sq_off_ids = await async_squareoff_all_positions_(interactive_client) print("Emergency Squared off Order IDs:", sq_off_ids) 10 Robust Code Design: Reconnections & Retries To deploy algorithms safely, you must handle network disconnects or API timeouts. Here is a production-grade template for a Gateway wrapper that you can copy to build your systems: import asyncio import logging from xts_api_client.xts_connect_async import XTSConnect from xts_api_client.interactive_socket import OrderSocket_io from xts_api_client.interactive_socket_client import InteractiveSocketClient from httpx import PoolTimeout, ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout class OrderCallbackHandler(InteractiveSocketClient): def __init__(self, gateway): self.gateway = gateway async def on_connect(self): self.gateway.connected = True logging.info("WebSocket connected!") async def on_disconnect(self): self.gateway.connected = False logging.warning("WebSocket lost! Reconnecting...") asyncio.create_task(self.gateway.reconnect()) class XTSGateway: def __init__(self, api_url, key, secret): self.api_url = api_url self.key = key self.secret = secret self.client = None self.socket = None self.connected = False async def connect(self): # 1. Login REST API self.client = XTSConnect(self.key, self.secret, "WEBAPI", self.api_url) await self.client.interactive_login() # 2. Start WebSocket Connection self.socket = OrderSocket_io( token=self.client.token, userID=self.client.userID, root_url=self.client.root, reconnection=True, interactiveSocketClient=OrderCallbackHandler(self) ) await self.socket.connect() async def place_order_safe(self, params: dict, retries=4): """Places orders with auto-retry on HTTP timeouts""" for attempt in range(retries): try: response = await self.client.place_order(**params) return response except (PoolTimeout, ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout) as timeout_exc: logging.warning(f"Timeout on attempt {attempt+1}/{retries}. Retrying...") await asyncio.sleep(0.5) raise RuntimeError("Failed to place order: Connection Timed Out")

docs.text: Authentication Authentication is the process of verifying who is making an API request before granting access to trading data and operations. Think of it like entering a secured building. Building = RMoney API Security Guard = Authentication System ID Card = API Key / Access Token Why Authentication is Required Protect user accounts from unauthorized use Prevent unauthorized access to trading APIs Secure all trading and order operations Keep financial data private and safe Track and audit API usage per application Authentication Components API Key Identifies your application to the RMoney server. RMY_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx Identifies the application Tracks API usage per app Blocks unauthorized applications API Secret Private key paired with your API Key for verification. xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx Never expose in frontend code. Store only in backend environment variables. Access Token Proves the logged-in user's identity on every request. eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs... Authenticates each API request Grants access to user resources Expires after 24 hours Authentication Flow Step-by-step process 1 Register your application on the portal 2 Get your API Key and API Secret 3 Call the Login API with credentials 4 Receive an Access Token in the response 5 Send the token in every API request header 6 Access API resources — place orders, fetch data Token validation inside the server Request Received Extract Token from Header Verify Token Signature Check Token Expiry Validate User Identity Allow Request to Proceed Login Request and Response Demo Request POST /interactive/user/session { "clientId": "RM12345", "password": "••••••••" } Demo Response { "type": "success", "result": { "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...", "userID": "RM12345", "isInvestorClient": false } } Using the Token Include the token in the Authorization header of every protected API call. No Bearer prefix is needed — send the raw token value. GET /interactive/portfolio/holdings Authorization: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs... GET /interactive/orders Authorization: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs... Authentication Errors Invalid Token { "error": "Invalid Token" } The token value is incorrect or malformed. Expired Token { "error": "Token Expired" } Token is valid but past its 24-hour lifetime. Refresh it. Unauthorized { "error": "Unauthorized" } No token was provided in the Authorization header. Security Best Practices Keep Secrets Secure Store API secrets only in backend environment variables. Never commit them to code repositories or expose them in frontend apps. Always Use HTTPS All API calls must use https:// . Plain HTTP exposes your token to network interception and man-in-the-middle attacks. Rotate Tokens Regularly Do not use the same token indefinitely. Refresh access tokens before they expire and immediately revoke compromised tokens. Validate Before Requesting Always check if your token is still valid before making an API call. Re-authenticate proactively instead of handling 401 errors reactively. Summary Component Purpose Where Used API Key Identifies your application Login request body API Secret Proves application authenticity Login request body Token Identifies the logged-in user Authorization header on every request Refresh Token Generates a new access token without re-login Token refresh endpoint

docs.text: Bracket Orders A Bracket Order (BO) combines three linked orders — Entry, Target, and Stop-Loss — into a single trade. Once the entry executes, the system automatically manages your exit for both profit and risk. Auto entry & exit Risk management Auto profit booking Stop-loss protection No constant monitoring Intraday leverage Components of a Bracket Order 1. Entry Order The first order used to enter the trade. Buy RELIANCE at ₹2,850 2. Target Order Profit booking — closes position when target price is reached. Target Price = ₹2,900 3. Stop-Loss Order Protective order — limits losses if market moves against the trade. Stop Loss = ₹2,830 How It Works Place Bracket Order → Entry Executed → Target & SL Created → Exit Triggered → Other Order Cancelled Example — RELIANCE 100 Shares Order Price Entry Price ₹2,850 Target Price ₹2,900 Stop-Loss Price ₹2,830 Scenario 1 — Profit Buy at ₹2,850 Price rises to ₹2,900 Target order executed Profit booked automatically Stop-loss order cancelled Scenario 2 — Loss Limited Buy at ₹2,850 Price falls to ₹2,830 Stop-loss order executed Position closed automatically Target order cancelled Bracket Order vs Cover Order COVER ORDER Entry + Stop-Loss only No profit target Only risk protection Best for mandatory stop-loss traders → BRACKET ORDER Entry + Target + Stop-Loss Auto profit booking at target Both profit & risk protection Best for predefined target & SL traders Advantages & Limitations Advantages Automatic profit booking Automatic stop-loss protection Better risk management No constant market monitoring All related orders placed together Higher intraday leverage available Limitations Mostly for intraday trading only Entry, target & SL are linked One exit cancels the other automatically Not supported on all instruments Exit depends on market conditions Common Use Cases 📈 Intraday Trading Open and close positions within the same trading day with automatic exits. 🛡️ Risk Management Automatically limit losses using a predefined stop-loss. 💰 Profit Booking Close the trade automatically when the target price is reached. 🤖 Automated Trading Manage positions without continuously watching the market. !!! tip Always set realistic target and stop-loss prices. Ensure sufficient margin before placing a Bracket Order, and verify the entry price before submitting. docs.text: Cover Orders A Cover Order (CO) is a special order that combines a main order with a compulsory stop-loss — giving you built-in risk protection and higher leverage in a single placement. Built-in stop-loss Higher leverage Automatic risk management Intraday trading Reduced monitoring Faster execution What is a Cover Order? A Cover Order lets you enter a trade with a mandatory stop-loss baked in. Because the broker knows your maximum possible loss upfront, they offer higher leverage — making CO ideal for active intraday traders who want capital efficiency without manual exit monitoring. Main Order Buys or sells the stock Executed immediately at market Entry price defined here Stop-Loss Order Placed automatically alongside Triggers if price moves against you Exits position to cap the loss How It Works — Example RELIANCE — BUY Cover Order ORDER DETAILS Buy Price ₹2,850 Stop Loss ₹2,830 Quantity 100 shares Max Risk ₹20 × 100 = ₹2,000 OUTCOMES Price rises → ₹2,900 Profit = ₹50 × 100 = ₹5,000 Price drops → ₹2,830 SL triggered — Loss capped at ₹2,000 Cover Order Workflow User Places Order → Main Order Executed → Stop-Loss Created → Market Moves → Profit or SL Triggered → Position Closed Features Mandatory Stop Loss Every CO must have a stop-loss. It cannot be placed without one. Higher Margin Benefit Because risk is predefined, brokers offer more leverage for Cover Orders. Automatic Risk Management Stop-loss triggers automatically — no need to manually watch the market. Intraday Only Cover Orders are squared off automatically before market close. Faster Execution Predefined risk parameters allow the system to execute orders more efficiently. docs.text: Data Types & Business Rules Data Types define what kind of value a field stores. Business Rules define how that data must behave — enforcing exchange and broker requirements to keep every request valid and consistent. Ensures valid data Consistent API requests Exchange compliant Prevents errors Broker validation Reduces trading errors Data Types Data Type Example Description String "RELIANCE" Text values Integer 100 Whole numbers Double 1250.50 Decimal numbers Boolean true True or false Array ["BUY", "SELL"] List of values Object { "price": 100 } Grouped fields Common Data Types in API Requests String Stores text values — exchange names, symbols, order sides. { "exchangeSegment": "NSECM" } Integer Stores whole numbers — quantities, instrument IDs. { "quantity": 100 } Double Stores decimal values — prices, stop loss levels. { "price": 2500.50 } Boolean Stores true/false flags — investor type, spread orders. { "isInvestorClient": true } Array Stores multiple values — order sides, segments. { "orderSide": ["BUY","SELL"] } Object Groups related fields — exchange info, nested configs. { "exchangeInfo": { "NSECM": { "productType": "MIS" } }} Business Rules Business rules are predefined validations that every request must satisfy before reaching the exchange. Examples Quantity Must Be Positive Quantity = 10 → Accepted Quantity = -5 → Rejected Price Must Be Greater Than Zero Price = 2500 → Accepted Price = 0 → Rejected Order Side Must Be BUY or SELL BUY / SELL → Accepted PURCHASE → Rejected Stop Loss Logic (BUY order) SL Price < Trigger < Limit Any other order → Rejected Common Business Rules Rule Description Quantity > 0 Quantity cannot be zero or negative Price > 0 Price must be greater than zero Valid Product Type Must be MIS, NRML, CNC, CO, or BO Valid Exchange Segment Exchange must exist and be active Market Hours Check Orders only during trading hours Margin Availability Sufficient funds must be available Authentication Required Valid session token required Valid Instrument Instrument must exist on the exchange How Validation Works User Request → Validate Data Types → Apply Business Rules → Broker Checks → Exchange Validation → Response Generated API Field Reference Field Name Data Type Size Description ClientID String 15 Client ID. docs.text: Exchange Messages Exchange Messages are official notifications sent by the stock exchange (such as NSE or BSE) to inform traders and brokers about important market events, trading updates, or system announcements. Official Notifications Real-time Alerts NSE & BSE Market Transparency What are Exchange Messages? Exchange Messages are official announcements from the exchange that provide important information related to trading, market operations, and system updates. They help users stay informed about anything that may affect trading activities. OFFICIAL SOURCE Directly from NSE, BSE, or other exchanges REAL-TIME Delivered instantly when the exchange publishes them ACTIONABLE Help traders make informed decisions instantly Why are Exchange Messages Important? Stay informed about market changes as they happen Know if trading is suspended or resumed for a stock Be aware of special trading sessions or extended hours Receive important operational updates from the exchange Avoid trading issues caused by exchange announcements Improve overall market transparency and trader confidence Common Types of Exchange Messages 1. Trading Halt The exchange temporarily stops trading for a particular stock or the entire market. NSE Notice: Trading in ABC Ltd. has been suspended until further notice. 2. Trading Resume The exchange announces that trading has started again after a halt. Trading in ABC Ltd. has resumed from 11:30 AM. 3. Market Holiday Notice The exchange informs participants about upcoming market holidays . The stock market will remain closed on 15th August due to Independence Day. 4. Corporate Action Information about company events — dividend, bonus shares, stock split, rights issue, merger. XYZ Ltd. has announced a 1:1 Bonus Issue. 5. Auction Notification The exchange announces auction sessions for unsettled trades. Auction session will begin at 2:00 PM. 6. System Maintenance The exchange notifies users about planned maintenance windows. Exchange systems will undergo maintenance from 6 PM to 8 PM. 7. Price Band Revision The exchange changes the upper or lower trading limits for a security. The price band for ABC Ltd. has been revised from 10% to 20%. 8. Market-Wide Circuit Breaker The exchange pauses all trading due to significant index movements. Trading halted for 45 minutes due to a market-wide circuit breaker. Exchange Message Flow Exchange (NSE / BSE) ▼ Generates Official Announcement ▼ Broker / API Receives Message ▼ Trading Platform Displays Message ▼ Trader Reads the Notification Where Are Exchange Messages Displayed? Notifications panel Exchange Messages section Trading terminal Broker dashboard Mobile trading app Real-Life Example You are planning to buy shares of ABC Ltd. Before placing your order, you receive this exchange message: ⚠ NSE Alert: Trading in ABC Ltd. has been suspended due to a pending corporate announcement. Since trading is temporarily halted, you cannot place or execute orders for that stock until the exchange resumes trading. The exchange message helps you avoid a failed order attempt and plan accordingly. Exchange Messages in Market Data API The Exchange Messages endpoint allows applications to retrieve official messages published by the exchange and display them directly to traders. Message Type Description Trading Halt Trading suspension notices for stocks or markets Trading Resume Trading restart announcements after a halt Market Holiday Exchange holiday notifications and closure dates Corporate Actions Dividend, bonus, stock split, rights issue, etc. Auction Notices Auction session timings and information System Maintenance Exchange maintenance windows and downtime Price Band Updates Changes in circuit limits or price bands General Announcements Other important exchange notifications In Simple Words: Exchange Messages are official announcements from the stock exchange that inform traders about important market events such as trading halts, market holidays, corporate actions, auctions, and system updates. They help traders stay informed and make better trading decisions. Exchange Message GET The exchange sends various messages to connected brokers, such as information about bans, circuit limits, and news about listed companies. Users can access messages relevant to them using this API. URL GET https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/1interactive/messages/exchange?exchangeSegment=NSECM Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment ↗ Y ExchangeSegment Response Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Description exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment ↗ ExchangeSegment ↗ ExchangeTimeStamp ExchangeTimeStamp ↗ Date and time provided by the exchange when a specific event or message was generated. BroadcastMessage BroadcastMessage Message Send by exchange Response Body JSON { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-messages-0001" , "description" : "Exchange messages" , "result" : { "messageList" : [ { "ExchangeSegment" : 2 , "ExchangeTimeStamp" : 1452777915 , "BroadcastMessage" : "Listing -> CORPORATE ANNOUNCEMENTS" , "SequenceId" : 1904678908069178 , "ExchangeInstrumentID" : 0 , "MessageCode" : 1506 , "MessageVersion" : 8 , "TokenID" : 0 , "ApplicationType" : 0 , "SequenceNumber" : 1904678908069177 } ] } } Copy Show Full Code Examples CURL Python curl --location "https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/1interactive/messages/exchange?exchangeSegment=NSECM" \ --header 'Authorization: xxxxxx' Copy import requests url = "https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/1interactive/messages/exchange?exchangeSegment=NSECM" payload = "" headers = { 'Authorization' : 'xxxxxx' } response = requests. request ( "GET" , url, headers=headers, data=payload) print (response.text) Copy Show Full package main import ( "fmt" "net/http" "io/ioutil" ) func main () { url := "https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/1interactive/messages/exchange?exchangeSegment=NSECM" client := &http.Client{} req , _ := http. docs.text: Exchange Status Exchange Status shows the current operating state of a stock exchange — whether it is open, closed, halted, or in a special trading session. It helps traders know if trading is currently allowed and what phase the market is in. Market Hours Live Status NSE, BSE & MCX Session Awareness What is Exchange Status? Exchange Status indicates whether a stock exchange is currently open, closed, or in a specific trading phase. Before placing any order, traders use this to confirm that trading is available and to understand which market session is currently active. MARKET PHASE Know which trading session is currently active ORDER SAFETY Avoid placing orders when trading is unavailable INTERRUPTIONS Stay informed about halts and special sessions Common Exchange Status Types 1. Open The exchange is open and trading is taking place normally . Exchange Status : OPEN Buy shares Sell shares Modify orders Cancel orders 2. Closed The exchange is not accepting trades — market has closed or it is a holiday. Exchange Status : CLOSED No trading is possible until the next trading session. 3. Pre-Open A session before regular market hours where orders can be placed but continuous trading has not started yet. Exchange Status : PRE-OPEN Orders can be entered/modified/cancelled. The exchange determines the opening price . 4. Post-Close A session after regular market hours where certain activities may still be allowed. Exchange Status : POST-CLOSE Depending on exchange rules, some order-related activities may still be available. 5. Trading Halt Trading has been temporarily suspended . Reasons may include: Corporate announcements Technical issues Regulatory actions Circuit breakers Exchange Status : HALTED 6. Auction Session A special session used for auction-related trading, such as settling short deliveries. Exchange Status : AUCTION Only auction-related trades are processed during this session. 7. Suspended Trading for a specific security has been suspended until further notice . No orders can be executed for that security until the exchange lifts the suspension. Exchange Status : SUSPENDED Exchange Status Lifecycle Market Closed ▼ Pre-Open Session ▼ Market Open ▼ (Optional) Trading Halt ▼ Trading Resumes ▼ Market Close ▼ Post-Close Session Example ⏰ 10:30 AM — Market Open Exchange : NSE Status : OPEN Session : Regular Trading You can place, modify, and cancel orders normally. ⏰ 3:30 PM — Market Closed Exchange : NSE Status : CLOSED Market has closed. New trades cannot be executed. Information Returned by Exchange Status API Field Description Exchange Name of the exchange (NSE, BSE, MCX, etc.) Status Current market status — Open, Closed, Halted, Auction, etc. Session Current trading session — Pre-Open, Regular, Auction, Post-Close Start Time Session start time End Time Session end time Last Updated Time when the status was last refreshed Why Trading Applications Use Exchange Status Enable or disable trading buttons based on market status Display market availability clearly to the user Prevent invalid order placement outside trading hours Inform users about market sessions and transitions Synchronize application behaviour with the exchange Real-Life Example You open a trading app at 8:45 AM . ⏰ 8:45 AM Exchange : NSE Status : PRE-OPEN You can place orders, but regular trading hasn't started yet. ⏰ 9:15 AM Exchange : NSE Status : OPEN Regular trading has begun. Orders can now be matched and executed . In Simple Words: Exchange Status tells you the current state of the stock exchange — such as Open, Closed, Pre-Open, Halted, or Auction — so you know whether trading is available and which market session is currently active. Exchange Status GET Exchange Status indicates the availability of eligible exchanges for normal trading. It allows users to determine whether they can place an order or not. docs.text: Enums with Numeric Constants Enums (Enumerations) are predefined sets of values used by the API to represent options, states, or configurations — using compact numeric codes for speed, consistency, and reduced payload. Faster processing Standardized values Reduced payload Prevents invalid values Less coding errors Easier validation What are Enums? Instead of sending long descriptive text, APIs use short codes internally. For example: WITHOUT ENUMS "productType": "Margin Intraday Square Off" → WITH ENUMS "productType": 1 where 1 = MIS How Enums Work Internally Send productType: 1 → API maps 1 = MIS → Broker processes intraday order → Response returned Best Practices Use enum names instead of hardcoding numbers # Avoid productType = 1 # Prefer productType = ProductType.MIS Validate values before sending ✔ BUY ✔ SELL ✖ PURCHASE ← not a valid enum value 1. Exchange Segments Enum Name Numeric Code Description NSECM 1 - NSE(National Stock Exchange)Cash Market - It is a normal buying/selling cash market in NSE. - Most of the traders trade here on thr regular basis. NSEFO 2 - NSE Futures & Options - Derivatives segment of NSE where equity futures, index futures, and options contracts are traded. - It is a market of future & options trading in NSE. NSECD 3 - NSE Currency - Currency trading segment at NSE for exchange-traded currency futures and options (USD/INR, EUR/INR, etc.) - It is a market of currency trading in NSE. BSECM 11 - BSE(Bombay Stock Exchange)Cash Market - Cash/equity segment of BSE, the oldest stock exchange in Asia, where stocks are bought and sold. - It is a normal buying/selling trades market in BSE. BSEFO 12 - BSE Futures & Options - Derivatives segment of BSE offering equity derivatives, index derivatives, and stock futures/options. - It is a Future & Options trade market in BSE BSECD 13 - BSE Currency Derivative - Currency derivatives platform of BSE that allows trading in exchange-listed currency futures and options. - It is a Currency trade market in BSE. MCXFO 51 - MCX(Multi Commodity Exchange)Future & Option - Derivatives trading segment of MCX for commodities such as gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas, and agricultural products. - It is a Commodity(e.g. Physical Goods/Products) trade market NCDEX 21 - National Commodity And Derivatives Exchange. - A leading exchange focused on agricultural commodity futures like soybean, chana, guar, and other agri-products. - It is a Agriculture Commodity Exchange market 2. ProductType Enum Name Numeric Code Description MIS 1 - Margin Intraday Square-off - Intraday trading product type where positions must be squared off before market close. Provides higher leverage compared to delivery. - MIS is used for same-day trading only called Intraday Trading. - All trades must be closed before the market closes (9:15 AM – 3:30 PM). - The broker gives extra money (leverage), so you can trade with a larger amount. - If you don't close the trade, the broker will automatically close it before market close. - After closing the trade, the broker takes back its money, and you keep your money along with any profit (or bear any loss). NRML 2 - Normal - Standard product type used for carrying forward positions overnight in derivatives or cash without compulsory intraday square-off. - NRML is used to keep trades overnight or for multiple days. - You do not need to close the trade on the same day. - It is mainly used for Futures and Options (F&O) trading. - You can hold the trade until the contract expiry date; after expiry, the position expires or is settled automatically. - Brokers also provide leverage in NRML, but it is usually lower than the leverage available in MIS. CNC 4 - Cash And Carry - Delivery-based product type for equity trades. Shares are delivered to the Demat account, with no leverage. - CNC is used for real stock delivery and long-term investing. - Trades are done using your own money, with little or no leverage. - It is mainly used for buying and selling shares (equity). - There is no need to close the position on the same day. - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years. CO 8 - Cover Order - CO is mainly used for intraday (same-day) trading. - Intraday order type where a market or limit order is placed along with a mandatory stop-loss order. Provides higher leverage while controlling risk. - It focuses on safety and risk control. - A stop-loss (loss limit) order is compulsory with every trade. - Brokers usually provide higher leverage because the risk is controlled. - If the market moves against you and reaches the stop-loss price, the trade is automatically exited to limit the loss. BO 16 - Bracket Order - Advanced order type where a main order is placed with both a target (profit booking) and stop-loss. Once one is executed, the other is automatically cancelled. Can also include a trailing stop-loss. - BO focuses on both profit target and stop-loss. - It is used to balance profit and loss automatically. - It contains three orders: Entry Order, Target Profit Order, and Stop-Loss Order. - When the market reaches either the target price or the stop-loss price, the trade exits automatically. - It is mainly used for intraday trading and helps traders manage risk and profit together. MTF 32 - Margin Trading Faciity - Allows investors to buy stocks by partly paying upfront and borrowing the balance from the broker. Shares can be carried forward as long as margin requirements are met. - MTF is used for buying shares with the help of money borrowed from the broker. - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount. - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years. - The borrowed amount remains with the broker, and interest is charged until it is repaid. - It allows you to buy more shares than you could using only your own money. 3. OrderType Enum Name Numeric Code Description Market 1 - Market Order - An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price in the market. - A Market Order is executed immediately at the current market price. - You only specify the quantity to buy or sell; the price is decided by the market. - It is used when quick execution is more important than getting a specific price. - Example: If TCS is trading around ₹3500 and you place a Market Buy Order, it will be executed immediately at the best available market price. Limit 2 - Limit Order - An order to buy or sell at a specified price (or better). - In a Limit Order, you set the price at which you want to buy or sell. - The trade is executed only if the market reaches your specified price or a better price. - It is used when getting a specific price is more important than immediate execution. - Example: If the current TCS price is ₹3500 and you place a Buy Limit Order at ₹3480, the order will execute only if TCS falls to ₹3480 or below; otherwise, it will remain pending. StopMarket 4 - StopMarket Order - An order that becomes a market order once a specified trigger price is reached. Used mainly to limit losses. - In a Stop Market Order, you set a trigger price (stop price). - When the market reaches the trigger price, the order becomes a Market Order and is executed immediately at the best available price. - It is mainly used to limit losses or protect profits automatically. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500 and set a Stop Market Sell Order with a trigger price of ₹3480, then when TCS falls to ₹3480, the order is activated and the shares are sold immediately at the current market price. StopLimit 8 - StopLimit Order - An order that becomes a limit order once the trigger price is reached. It executes only at the specified limit price or better. - In a Stop Limit Order, you set both a trigger price and a limit price. - When the market reaches the trigger price, a Limit Order is placed at the specified limit price. - It is used to control the execution price while limiting losses or protecting profits. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500, you can set a trigger price of ₹3480 and a limit price of ₹3475. When TCS reaches ₹3480, a sell order at ₹3475 is placed. The trade will execute only at ₹3475 or a better price. OCO 32 - One Cancels the Other - A conditional order where two linked orders are placed — if one gets executed, the other is automatically cancelled. - OCO contains two orders together, usually a Target Order and a Stop-Loss Order. - It helps you manage both profit and loss automatically. - When one order is executed, the other order is automatically cancelled. - It is useful when you want to set both a profit target and a loss limit without monitoring the market continuously. MTF 32 - Margin Trading Facility - MTF allows you to buy shares using money borrowed from the broker. - You can hold the shares for a long time (days, months, or years); there is no need to close the trade on the same day - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount until it is repaid. - It helps you buy more shares than you could with only your own money. 4. OrderSide Enum Name Numeric Code Description BUY 49 - BUY means purchasing a stock or contract. - Indicates a purchase transaction. Used when entering a long position (expecting the price to rise). - You buy when you expect the price to go up. - Profit is made if you sell later at a higher price. SELL 50 - SELL means selling a stock or contract. - Indicates a sale transaction. Used when exiting a long position or initiating a short position (expecting the price to fall). - You sell when you expect the price to go down or when you want to book profit. - Profit is made if you buy back later at a lower price (short selling) or if you sell shares you already own at a higher price. 5. TimeInForce Enum Name Numeric Code Description DAY 1 - Day Order - The order remains active only for the current trading day. - If the order is not executed by market close, it is automatically cancelled. - Order remains valid only for the trading day. If not executed by market close, it is cancelled automatically. GTC 2 - Good Till Cancelled - The order remains active until you cancel it manually. - It can stay active for many days if it is not executed. - The order is cancelled only when you manually cancel it. IOC 4 - Immediate Or Cancel - The order must be executed immediately. - If only some quantity can be executed, the remaining quantity is cancelled instantly. - Any unfilled part of the order does not stay pending. - Example: If you place an IOC order to buy 100 shares and only 60 shares are available, those 60 shares are bought immediately and the remaining 40 shares are cancelled. GTD 8 - Good Till Date - The order remains active until a specific date set by you. - It can stay active for many days until that date. - If the order is not executed by the specified date, it is automatically cancelled. EOS 16 - End Of Session - The order remains active only until the end of the current trading session (market day). - The order must be executed before the session ends. - If the order is not executed by the end of the session, it is automatically cancelled. COL 32 - Close of Trading Session - COL means the order is intended to be executed near the market closing time. - It helps traders place orders based on the closing price of the trading session. - The order is processed during the market closing period. GTDYS 128 - Good Till Defined Yielding Sessions - The order remains active for a predefined number of trading sessions. - It stays active across multiple market days until the defined session limit is reached. - If the order is not executed within those sessions, it is automatically cancelled. 6. Order Status Enum Name Numeric Code Description Open or New 48 - Open/New means a new order has been placed and is waiting to be executed. - The order is active in the market but has not been fully or partially traded yet. - The order can later be executed, modified, or cancelled. PartiallyFilled 49 - PartiallyFilled Order - It means only some part of the order has been executed.The remaining quantity is still active and waiting to be executed. - The order stays open until the remaining quantity is filled or cancelled. Filled 50 - Filled Order - Filled means the order has been completely executed. - All the requested quantity has been bought or sold successfully. Cancelled 52 - Cancelled Order - Cancelled means the order has been cancelled and will not be executed. - The order may be cancelled by you, the broker, or the exchange. - No quantity will be traded after the order is cancelled. Replaced 53 - Replaced Order - Replaced means an existing order has been modified or updated. - The old order is replaced with a new one having the updated details.Changes may include price, quantity, or other order parameters. PendingCancel 54 - PendingCancel Order - PendingCancel means a cancellation request has been sent, but the order has not been cancelled yet. - The system or exchange is processing the cancellation request.The order status will change to Cancelled once the cancellation is completed. Rejected 56 - Rejected Order - Rejected means the order was not accepted by the exchange or broker. - The order is not executed and becomes inactive. - Common reasons include insufficient funds, invalid price, or trading restrictions. PendingNew 65 - PendingNew Order - PendingNew means the order has been received but has not yet become active in the market. - The exchange or broker is still processing the order.Once processing is complete, the status changes to Open/New. PendingReplace 69 - PendingReplace Order - PendingReplace means a request to modify an existing order has been sent, but the changes have not been applied yet. - The exchange or broker is still processing the modification request. - Once the modification is completed, the order status changes to Replaced. 7. Order Source Enum Name Numeric Code Description TWS 1 - Trader Workstation - TWS refers to a trading terminal or trading platform used to place and manage orders. - It provides access to market data and trading features. - Traders can buy, sell, modify, and monitor orders through TWS. - Example: A trader using a desktop trading application to place an order for 100 TCS shares is using a TWS (Trader Workstation). TWSAPI 2 - Trader Workstation API - TWSAPI means orders are placed programmatically through an API instead of manually. - It allows applications or trading algorithms to connect directly to the trading platform. - Orders can be placed, modified, and monitored automatically using code. - Example: A Python program that automatically buys 100 TCS shares through the broker's API is using TWSAPI. WEB 21 - WEB means the order was placed through a web-based trading platform or website. - Orders entered manually by the trader through the broker's web-based trading platform. - It indicates that the source of the order is the broker's web application. - Traders can place, modify, and monitor orders using a browser. - Example: If you log in to your broker's website and buy 100 TCS shares, the order source will be WEB. WEBAPI 22 - WEBAPI means the order was placed through a web-based API, not manually through the website. - It allows applications or programs to place and manage orders automatically. - It allows applications or programs to place and manage orders automatically. - Example: A Python script using a broker's REST API to buy 100 TCS shares is using WEBAPI. MOBILEANDROID 41 - MOBILEANDROID means the order was placed using the broker's Android mobile app. - It indicates that the source of the order is an Android device. - Traders can place, modify, and track orders through the mobile app. - Example: If you use your Android phone to buy 100 TCS shares through the broker's app, the order source will be MOBILEANDROID. MOBILEIOS 81 - MOBILEIOS means the order was placed using the broker's iPhone or iPad app. - It indicates that the source of the order is an iOS device. - Traders can place, modify, and track orders through the mobile app. - Example: If you use your iPhone to buy 100 TCS shares through the broker's app, the order source will be MOBILEIOS. EnterpriseWeb 154 - EnterpriseWeb means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional web platform. - It is typically used by organizations, brokers, or large clients rather than individual retail traders. - Orders can be placed and managed through a specialized web-based interface. - Example: If a mutual fund or a corporate client places an order through the broker's enterprise web portal, the order source will be EnterpriseWeb. EnterpriseMobile 155 - EnterpriseMobile means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional mobile application. - It is mainly used by organizations, brokers, or large clients, not regular retail traders. - Orders can be placed and managed through a specialized mobile platform. - Example: If a mutual fund manager places an order using the broker's enterprise mobile app, the order source will be EnterpriseMobile. EnterpriseTWS 156 - EnterpriseTWS means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional trading workstation (TWS). - It is mainly used by organizations, brokers, or large clients rather than individual retail traders. - Orders can be placed, modified, and monitored through a professional trading terminal. - Example: If a mutual fund or a brokerage firm places an order using its enterprise trading workstation, the order source will be EnterpriseTWS. 8. Position Square Off Mode Enum Name Numeric Code Description DayWise 1 - DayWise means positions or statistics are calculated separately for each trading day. - Only the trades done on the current day are considered. - At the end of the day, the values are reset for the next trading day. - Example: If you buy and sell 100 TCS shares today, the profit/loss will be shown only for today's trades under DayWise.** NetWise 2 - NetWise means all trades are combined together to show the overall (net) position. - It considers both previous and current trades instead of only today's trades. - It shows your total quantity, average price, and overall profit/loss. - Example: If you bought 100 TCS shares yesterday and 50 more today, NetWise will show a total position of 150 shares.** 9. Position Square Off Quantity Type Enum Name Numeric Code Description Percentage 0 - Percentage means values are shown in percentage (%) instead of actual numbers. - It helps compare profit, loss, growth, or performance easily. - The result is displayed as a percentage of the total value. ExactQty 1 - ExactQty means the exact quantity requested must be executed. - The order will not be partially filled. - If the full quantity is not available, the order may remain pending or fail based on the order rules. 10. MarketType Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1 - Normal means regular trading. - It is the standard order type used for normal buy and sell transactions. - No special conditions or restrictions are applied to the order. Oddlot 2 - It means the order is an odd lot type - It is used when quantity is less than the standard trading lot size - These are small or non-standard share quantities (not full lots) - It is treated separately from normal lot trading in the system.Useful for small quantity or partial share trading orders - Example: • Suppose the normal trading lot size is 100 shares • A trader places an order for 25 shares of Reliance Industries • Since 25 is less than the standard lot size (100), it is treated as an Odd Lot order • In the system/API, this order will be marked as: Oddlot = 2 RetailDebt 3 - represents a retail debt order type - It is used for buying/selling debt instruments like bonds or government securities - These trades are done by retail (individual) investors, not big institutions - It usually involves small investment amounts Auction 4 - represents orders placed in an auction market - It is used when securities are traded through a bidding process instead of normal trading - Buyers and sellers submit bids, and the best price gets matched - It is often used in special cases like exchange auctions or settlement auctions CallAuction1 5 - represents a specific call auction order type (Phase 1) - Used to find a single fair market price by matching many buy and sell orders at once. - Orders are first collected, then the system calculates one price, and finally trades are executed together in one batch. CallAuction2 6 - means a second type of call auction session where orders are not executed instantly. - Orders are first collected and then a single fair price is discovered by the system. - After price discovery, all matching buy and sell orders are executed together in one batch. - it is a batch trading mode where trades happen together at one final auction price. 11. OrderLegStatus Enum Name Numeric Code Description SingleOrderLeg 1 - means the order contains only one trading instruction (one leg). - It is a regular standalone order, not part of a multi-leg strategy. - The order is executed independently without being linked to other orders. - In simple words: one order = one action (buy or sell) on a single instrument. SpreadFirstLeg 2 - means this order is the first leg of a spread strategy. - A spread strategy consists of two or more linked orders executed together. - The first leg is the initial buy or sell order in the spread. - Example: Buy NIFTY July Futures (first leg) and Sell NIFTY August Futures (second leg). SpreadSecondLeg 3 - means this order is the second leg of a spread strategy. - It is linked to the first leg and forms part of a multi-leg trade. - Both legs work together to implement a spread trading strategy. MultilegFirstLeg 4 - means this order is the first leg of a multi-leg trading strategy. - A multi-leg strategy contains two or more linked orders that work together. - This is the starting order of the strategy, followed by additional legs. - Example: Buy a Call Option as the first leg of an options strategy. MultilegSecondLeg 5 - means this order is the second leg of a multi-leg trading strategy. - It is linked to the first leg and helps complete the overall strategy. - Multiple legs are used together to achieve a specific trading objective. MultilegThirdLeg 6 - means this order is the third leg of a multi-leg trading strategy. - It is linked with the first and second legs as part of the same strategy. - Multi-leg strategies use several connected orders to achieve a trading goal. 12. Bo_Leg_Details Enum Name Numeric Code Description EntryLeg 1 - indicates that this order is the entry (starting) leg of a trading strategy. - It is the first order placed to open or initiate a position before any related exit or adjustment orders. ProfitTargetExitLeg 2 - indicates that this order is used to exit a position when the desired profit target is reached. - It helps automatically close the trade and lock in profits once the specified target price is achieved. StoplossExitLeg 3 - indicates that this order is used to exit a position when the price reaches a predefined loss limit. - It helps reduce potential losses by automatically closing the trade when the stop-loss price is triggered. \ 13. DayOrNet Enum Name Numeric Code Description DAY 1 - means the order remains active only for the current trading day. - If the order is not executed by the end of the trading session, it is automatically cancelled. NET 2 - means the position is viewed and managed on a net basis, where all buy and sell trades are combined into a single net position. - Includes delivery trades (CNC) or carry-forward derivative positions (NRML). - For example, if you buy 100 shares and sell 40 shares, your net position becomes 60 shares long. 14. InstrumentType Enum Name Numeric Code Description Futures 1 - Futures are contracts to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a future date. - They are commonly used for hedging risk or speculating on price movements. - Standardized derivative contracts to buy or sell an asset (stock, index, commodity, or currency) at a predetermined price on a future date. Options 2 - Options are contracts that give the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a specified price before expiry. - They are used for hedging and advanced trading strategies. - Derivative contracts that give the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy (Call) or sell (Put) the underlying asset at a fixed price within a specified time. Spread 4 - Spread is a trading strategy involving two or more related positions taken together. - It aims to profit from the price difference between the instruments. - A strategy involving simultaneous buying and selling of related instruments. Equity 8 - Equity represents ownership shares in a company. - Investors buy and sell equities to participate in the company's growth and returns. - Shares of listed companies traded in the cash market segment. Spot 16 - Spot refers to the immediate purchase or sale of a financial instrument at the current market price. - Settlement usually occurs within the standard exchange settlement cycle. - Trades for immediate delivery and settlement at the current market price, typically used in currencies and commodities. PreferenceShares 32 - Preference Shares are shares that provide priority in dividend payments over common equity shares. - They generally have fixed dividends but limited voting rights. - A class of shares that provides fixed dividends and has priority over equity shares in dividend distribution and liquidation, but usually with limited voting rights. Debentures 64 - Debentures are debt instruments issued by companies to raise funds from investors. - They pay fixed interest and are repaid on a specified maturity date. - Long-term debt instruments issued by companies or governments to raise funds. Typically carry fixed interest payments. Warrants 128 - Warrants are financial instruments that give the holder the right to buy a company's shares at a fixed price before a certain date. - They are often issued along with bonds or other securities. - Financial instruments that give the holder the right to buy equity shares at a specific price before a set expiry date. Miscellaneous 256 - Miscellaneous includes financial instruments that do not fall under standard categories. - It serves as a generic classification for special or uncommon instruments. - Category for instruments that do not fall into standard classifications (used for special or rare products). MutualFund 512 - Mutual Fund is an investment vehicle that pools money from multiple investors and invests in a diversified portfolio. - It is managed by professional fund managers on behalf of investors. - Units of pooled investment schemes managed by Asset Management Companies (AMCs). 15. TradingSession Enum Name Numeric Code Description PreOpenStart 0 - Indicates the start of the Pre-Open Market session. - During this phase, traders can place, modify, or cancel orders. - No trades are executed yet. - The beginning of the pre-open session where orders can be placed but are not matched immediately. PreOpenEnd 1 - Indicates the end of the Pre-Open Market session. - The system finalizes price discovery based on collected orders. - Trading is about to move to the normal market session. - The end of the pre-open session when accumulated orders are matched and the opening price is determined. NormalStart 2 - Indicates the start of the regular trading session. - Orders are matched and executed continuously. - Normal buying and selling begins. - The start of the regular trading session where continuous matching of buy and sell orders happens. NormalEnd 4 - Indicates the end of the regular trading session. - No new trades are executed after market close. -Remaining unexecuted DAY orders are cancelled. - The close of the regular trading session; after this point, no further trades are executed in the normal market. PreClosingStart 8 - Indicates the start of the Pre-Closing session. - Used to determine the closing price of securities. - Orders may be collected for closing price calculation. - The start of the pre-closing session, where the system collects data to calculate the closing price (closing auction). PreClosingEnd 16 - Indicates the end of the Pre-Closing session. - The final closing price is determined. - Market moves toward complete closure. - The end of the pre-closing session when the official closing price is determined and published. 16. ValuationType Enum Name Numeric Code Description NONE 0 - No valuation method is applied. - The position or instrument is not valued using a specific calculation. - Used when valuation is not required. - Default flag when no special settlement type is applied. The order follows the normal market settlement rules. CL 1 - Valuation is based on the Closing Price. - The last closing market price is used for calculation. - Commonly used for end-of-day valuations. - Orders specifically placed to be executed at the market's closing price during the closing session. LT 2 - Commonly used for end-of-day valuations. - Commonly used for end-of-day valuations. - Reflects the current market value more closely. - Segment used for block deals, bulk trades, or special limited trading windows defined by the exchange. 17. HoldingType Enum Name Numeric Code Description T1_Holdings 1 - Shares purchased today but not yet settled. - These shares are waiting to be credited to the Demat account. - Usually become regular holdings after settlement. - Securities bought but not yet fully settled (i.e., on T+1 day). Holdings 3 - Shares that are fully settled and available in the Demat account. - Can be sold or held as a long-term investment. - Represents regular stock holdings. - Fully settled securities that are credited to the client's Demat account. MTFHoldings 3 - Shares purchased through the Margin Trading Facility (MTF). - The broker provides funding for part of the purchase value. - Investors can take larger positions using margin. Securities purchased under Margin Trading Facility where part of the funds are borrowed from the broker. 18. StatisticsLevel Enum Name Numeric Code Description ParentLevel 0 - Represents the main or top-level statistics category. - Used to group related statistical data together. - Acts as the parent for one or more child levels. - Represents the top-level entity in a hierarchy. ChildLevel 1 - Represents a sub-category under a parent level. - Contains detailed statistics related to the parent category. - Used for more granular data analysis. - Represents a sub-entity under a parent. 19. Socket Event Enum Name Description joined - Indicates that the socket connection has been established successfully. - The client is now connected and ready to receive data. - Sent when a user joins the socket session. - Sent when a client successfully connects and joins the WebSocket channel. Confirms that the real-time stream is active. error - Indicates that an error occurred during the socket operation. - The requested action could not be completed successfully. - Usually includes error details or a message. - Indicates a failure or issue (e.g., invalid request, authentication failure, or system error). Requires client-side handling. warning - Indicates a non-critical issue or alert. - The connection is still active, but attention may be required. - Used to notify about potential problems. - Non-critical issue or advisory message (e.g., rate-limit approaching, deprecated API usage). success - Indicates that an operation completed successfully. - Confirms that the requested action was processed. - Usually returned after a successful request. - Confirms that a client request was processed successfully (e.g., order placement acknowledged). order - Indicates an order-related event. - Used to send updates about order placement or status changes. - Helps track order activity in real time. - Event carrying real-time updates about an order lifecycle — placed, modified, filled, cancelled, or rejected. trade - Indicates a trade execution event. - Sent when an order is matched and executed. - Provides trade details and execution information. - Sent when an order results in an actual trade execution (full or partial). Contains trade ID, price, and quantity details. logout - Indicates that the user has been disconnected or logged out. - The socket session is closed. - No further updates will be received until reconnection. - Notification that the session or WebSocket connection has been terminated — either manually or due to token expiry. position - Indicates a position-related update. - Sent when there is a change in the user's holdings or positions. - Helps track open positions in real time. - Real-time updates about portfolio positions, including intraday (DayWise) or carry-forward (NetWise) quantities. tradeConversion - Indicates a trade conversion event. - Sent when a trade or position is converted from one product type to another. - Example: Converting MIS to CNC. - Event triggered when an order/trade is converted from one product type to another (e.g., Intraday MIS → Delivery CNC). gttOrder - Indicates a request or response for order details. - Used to fetch information about existing orders. - Returns order-related data. - Event update for GTT Orders (orders that activate only when a trigger price is met). gttOrderRejection - Indicates an order rejection event or request. - Sent when an order is rejected by the system or exchange. - Provides the reason for rejection. - Notification when a GTT Order fails to activate due to invalid conditions, margin shortfall, or exchange rejection. 20. Order Session Type Enum Name Numeric Code Description AMO 1 - AMO (After Market Order) allows orders to be placed after market hours. - The order is sent to the exchange when the market opens. - Useful when you cannot place orders during trading hours. - Standard market order placed during regular market hours. OT 2 - OT (Order Through Trading Hours) indicates a regular order placed during market hours. - The order is sent directly to the exchange for execution. - Used for normal day-to-day trading. - After Market Order — Orders placed after market hours to be processed when the market opens. INSTI 4 - INSTI indicates that the order is placed by an institutional investor. - Typically used by banks, mutual funds, or large financial institutions. - Such orders are usually larger in size than retail orders. - Institutional — Orders placed through institutional trading sessions. GTT 5 - GTT (Good Till Triggered) is an order that remains active until a specified trigger price is reached. - The order is automatically placed when the trigger condition is met. - Useful for long-term buy or sell targets. - Good Till Triggered — Order remains pending until the trigger condition is met.

NSEFO 2 - NSE Futures & Options - Derivatives segment of NSE where equity futures, index futures, and options contracts are traded. - It is a market of future & options trading in NSE. BSEFO 12 - BSE Futures & Options - Derivatives segment of BSE offering equity derivatives, index derivatives, and stock futures/options. - It is a Future & Options trade market in BSE BSECD 13 - BSE Currency Derivative - Currency derivatives platform of BSE that allows trading in exchange-listed currency futures and options. - It is a Currency trade market in BSE. MCXFO 51 - MCX(Multi Commodity Exchange)Future & Option - Derivatives trading segment of MCX for commodities such as gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas, and agricultural products. - It is a Commodity(e.g. Physical Goods/Products) trade market NCDEX 21 - National Commodity And Derivatives Exchange. - A leading exchange focused on agricultural commodity futures like soybean, chana, guar, and other agri-products. - It is a Agriculture Commodity Exchange market
