Provides higher leverage compared to delivery. - MIS is used for same-day trading only called Intraday Trading. - All trades must be closed before the market closes (9:15 AM – 3:30 PM). - The broker gives extra money (leverage), so you can trade with a larger amount. - If you don't close the trade, the broker will automatically close it before market close. - After closing the trade, the broker takes back its money, and you keep your money along with any profit (or bear any loss). NRML 2 - Normal - Standard product type used for carrying forward positions overnight in derivatives or cash without compulsory intraday square-off. - NRML is used to keep trades overnight or for multiple days. - You do not need to close the trade on the same day. - It is mainly used for Futures and Options (F&O) trading. - You can hold the trade until the contract expiry date; after expiry, the position expires or is settled automatically. - Brokers also provide leverage in NRML, but it is usually lower than the leverage available in MIS. CNC 4 - Cash And Carry - Delivery-based product type for equity trades. Shares are delivered to the Demat account, with no leverage. - CNC is used for real stock delivery and long-term investing. - Trades are done using your own money, with little or no leverage. - It is mainly used for buying and selling shares (equity). - There is no need to close the position on the same day. - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years. CO 8 - Cover Order - CO is mainly used for intraday (same-day) trading. - Intraday order type where a market or limit order is placed along with a mandatory stop-loss order. Provides higher leverage while controlling risk. - It focuses on safety and risk control. - A stop-loss (loss limit) order is compulsory with every trade. - Brokers usually provide higher leverage because the risk is controlled. - If the market moves against you and reaches the stop-loss price, the trade is automatically exited to limit the loss. BO 16 - Bracket Order - Advanced order type where a main order is placed with both a target (profit booking) and stop-loss. Once one is executed, the other is automatically cancelled. Can also include a trailing stop-loss. - BO focuses on both profit target and stop-loss. - It is used to balance profit and loss automatically. - It contains three orders: Entry Order, Target Profit Order, and Stop-Loss Order. - When the market reaches either the target price or the stop-loss price, the trade exits automatically. - It is mainly used for intraday trading and helps traders manage risk and profit together. MTF 32 - Margin Trading Faciity - Allows investors to buy stocks by partly paying upfront and borrowing the balance from the broker. Shares can be carried forward as long as margin requirements are met. - MTF is used for buying shares with the help of money borrowed from the broker. - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount. - You can hold the shares for as long as you want, such as days, months, or even years. - The borrowed amount remains with the broker, and interest is charged until it is repaid. - It allows you to buy more shares than you could using only your own money.
docs.title: 2. ProductType

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Market 1 - Market Order - An order to buy or sell immediately at the best available price in the market. - A Market Order is executed immediately at the current market price. - You only specify the quantity to buy or sell; the price is decided by the market. - It is used when quick execution is more important than getting a specific price. - Example: If TCS is trading around ₹3500 and you place a Market Buy Order, it will be executed immediately at the best available market price. Limit 2 - Limit Order - An order to buy or sell at a specified price (or better). - In a Limit Order, you set the price at which you want to buy or sell. - The trade is executed only if the market reaches your specified price or a better price. - It is used when getting a specific price is more important than immediate execution. - Example: If the current TCS price is ₹3500 and you place a Buy Limit Order at ₹3480, the order will execute only if TCS falls to ₹3480 or below; otherwise, it will remain pending. StopMarket 4 - StopMarket Order - An order that becomes a market order once a specified trigger price is reached. Used mainly to limit losses. - In a Stop Market Order, you set a trigger price (stop price). - When the market reaches the trigger price, the order becomes a Market Order and is executed immediately at the best available price. - It is mainly used to limit losses or protect profits automatically. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500 and set a Stop Market Sell Order with a trigger price of ₹3480, then when TCS falls to ₹3480, the order is activated and the shares are sold immediately at the current market price. StopLimit 8 - StopLimit Order - An order that becomes a limit order once the trigger price is reached. It executes only at the specified limit price or better. - In a Stop Limit Order, you set both a trigger price and a limit price. - When the market reaches the trigger price, a Limit Order is placed at the specified limit price. - It is used to control the execution price while limiting losses or protecting profits. - Example: If you bought TCS at ₹3500, you can set a trigger price of ₹3480 and a limit price of ₹3475. When TCS reaches ₹3480, a sell order at ₹3475 is placed. The trade will execute only at ₹3475 or a better price. OCO 32 - One Cancels the Other - A conditional order where two linked orders are placed — if one gets executed, the other is automatically cancelled. - OCO contains two orders together, usually a Target Order and a Stop-Loss Order. - It helps you manage both profit and loss automatically. - When one order is executed, the other order is automatically cancelled. - It is useful when you want to set both a profit target and a loss limit without monitoring the market continuously. MTF 32 - Margin Trading Facility - MTF allows you to buy shares using money borrowed from the broker. - You can hold the shares for a long time (days, months, or years); there is no need to close the trade on the same day - The broker charges interest on the borrowed amount until it is repaid. - It helps you buy more shares than you could with only your own money.
docs.title: 3. OrderType

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description BUY 49 - BUY means purchasing a stock or contract. - Indicates a purchase transaction. Used when entering a long position (expecting the price to rise). - You buy when you expect the price to go up. - Profit is made if you sell later at a higher price. SELL 50 - SELL means selling a stock or contract. - Indicates a sale transaction. Used when exiting a long position or initiating a short position (expecting the price to fall). - You sell when you expect the price to go down or when you want to book profit. - Profit is made if you buy back later at a lower price (short selling) or if you sell shares you already own at a higher price.
docs.title: 4. OrderSide

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description DAY 1 - Day Order - The order remains active only for the current trading day. - If the order is not executed by market close, it is automatically cancelled. - Order remains valid only for the trading day. If not executed by market close, it is cancelled automatically. GTC 2 - Good Till Cancelled - The order remains active until you cancel it manually. - It can stay active for many days if it is not executed. - The order is cancelled only when you manually cancel it. IOC 4 - Immediate Or Cancel - The order must be executed immediately. - If only some quantity can be executed, the remaining quantity is cancelled instantly. - Any unfilled part of the order does not stay pending. - Example: If you place an IOC order to buy 100 shares and only 60 shares are available, those 60 shares are bought immediately and the remaining 40 shares are cancelled. GTD 8 - Good Till Date - The order remains active until a specific date set by you. - It can stay active for many days until that date. - If the order is not executed by the specified date, it is automatically cancelled. EOS 16 - End Of Session - The order remains active only until the end of the current trading session (market day). - The order must be executed before the session ends. - If the order is not executed by the end of the session, it is automatically cancelled. COL 32 - Close of Trading Session - COL means the order is intended to be executed near the market closing time. - It helps traders place orders based on the closing price of the trading session. - The order is processed during the market closing period. GTDYS 128 - Good Till Defined Yielding Sessions - The order remains active for a predefined number of trading sessions. - It stays active across multiple market days until the defined session limit is reached. - If the order is not executed within those sessions, it is automatically cancelled.
docs.title: 5. TimeInForce

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Open or New 48 - Open/New means a new order has been placed and is waiting to be executed. - The order is active in the market but has not been fully or partially traded yet. - The order can later be executed, modified, or cancelled. PartiallyFilled 49 - PartiallyFilled Order - It means only some part of the order has been executed.The remaining quantity is still active and waiting to be executed. - The order stays open until the remaining quantity is filled or cancelled. Filled 50 - Filled Order - Filled means the order has been completely executed. - All the requested quantity has been bought or sold successfully. Cancelled 52 - Cancelled Order - Cancelled means the order has been cancelled and will not be executed. - The order may be cancelled by you, the broker, or the exchange. - No quantity will be traded after the order is cancelled. Replaced 53 - Replaced Order - Replaced means an existing order has been modified or updated. - The old order is replaced with a new one having the updated details.Changes may include price, quantity, or other order parameters. PendingCancel 54 - PendingCancel Order - PendingCancel means a cancellation request has been sent, but the order has not been cancelled yet. - The system or exchange is processing the cancellation request.The order status will change to Cancelled once the cancellation is completed. Rejected 56 - Rejected Order - Rejected means the order was not accepted by the exchange or broker. - The order is not executed and becomes inactive. - Common reasons include insufficient funds, invalid price, or trading restrictions. PendingNew 65 - PendingNew Order - PendingNew means the order has been received but has not yet become active in the market. - The exchange or broker is still processing the order.Once processing is complete, the status changes to Open/New. PendingReplace 69 - PendingReplace Order - PendingReplace means a request to modify an existing order has been sent, but the changes have not been applied yet. - The exchange or broker is still processing the modification request. - Once the modification is completed, the order status changes to Replaced.

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description TWS 1 - Trader Workstation - TWS refers to a trading terminal or trading platform used to place and manage orders. - It provides access to market data and trading features. - Traders can buy, sell, modify, and monitor orders through TWS. - Example: A trader using a desktop trading application to place an order for 100 TCS shares is using a TWS (Trader Workstation). TWSAPI 2 - Trader Workstation API - TWSAPI means orders are placed programmatically through an API instead of manually. - It allows applications or trading algorithms to connect directly to the trading platform. - Orders can be placed, modified, and monitored automatically using code. - Example: A Python program that automatically buys 100 TCS shares through the broker's API is using TWSAPI. WEB 21 - WEB means the order was placed through a web-based trading platform or website. - Orders entered manually by the trader through the broker's web-based trading platform. - It indicates that the source of the order is the broker's web application. - Traders can place, modify, and monitor orders using a browser. - Example: If you log in to your broker's website and buy 100 TCS shares, the order source will be WEB. WEBAPI 22 - WEBAPI means the order was placed through a web-based API, not manually through the website. - It allows applications or programs to place and manage orders automatically. - It allows applications or programs to place and manage orders automatically. - Example: A Python script using a broker's REST API to buy 100 TCS shares is using WEBAPI. MOBILEANDROID 41 - MOBILEANDROID means the order was placed using the broker's Android mobile app. - It indicates that the source of the order is an Android device. - Traders can place, modify, and track orders through the mobile app. - Example: If you use your Android phone to buy 100 TCS shares through the broker's app, the order source will be MOBILEANDROID. MOBILEIOS 81 - MOBILEIOS means the order was placed using the broker's iPhone or iPad app. - It indicates that the source of the order is an iOS device. - Traders can place, modify, and track orders through the mobile app. - Example: If you use your iPhone to buy 100 TCS shares through the broker's app, the order source will be MOBILEIOS. EnterpriseWeb 154 - EnterpriseWeb means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional web platform. - It is typically used by organizations, brokers, or large clients rather than individual retail traders. - Orders can be placed and managed through a specialized web-based interface. - Example: If a mutual fund or a corporate client places an order through the broker's enterprise web portal, the order source will be EnterpriseWeb. EnterpriseMobile 155 - EnterpriseMobile means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional mobile application. - It is mainly used by organizations, brokers, or large clients, not regular retail traders. - Orders can be placed and managed through a specialized mobile platform. - Example: If a mutual fund manager places an order using the broker's enterprise mobile app, the order source will be EnterpriseMobile. EnterpriseTWS 156 - EnterpriseTWS means the order was placed through an enterprise or institutional trading workstation (TWS). - It is mainly used by organizations, brokers, or large clients rather than individual retail traders. - Orders can be placed, modified, and monitored through a professional trading terminal. - Example: If a mutual fund or a brokerage firm places an order using its enterprise trading workstation, the order source will be EnterpriseTWS.

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description DayWise 1 - DayWise means positions or statistics are calculated separately for each trading day. - Only the trades done on the current day are considered. - At the end of the day, the values are reset for the next trading day. - Example: If you buy and sell 100 TCS shares today, the profit/loss will be shown only for today's trades under DayWise.** NetWise 2 - NetWise means all trades are combined together to show the overall (net) position. - It considers both previous and current trades instead of only today's trades. - It shows your total quantity, average price, and overall profit/loss. - Example: If you bought 100 TCS shares yesterday and 50 more today, NetWise will show a total position of 150 shares.**
docs.title: 8. Position Square Off Mode

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Percentage 0 - Percentage means values are shown in percentage (%) instead of actual numbers. - It helps compare profit, loss, growth, or performance easily. - The result is displayed as a percentage of the total value. ExactQty 1 - ExactQty means the exact quantity requested must be executed. - The order will not be partially filled. - If the full quantity is not available, the order may remain pending or fail based on the order rules.

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1 - Normal means regular trading. - It is the standard order type used for normal buy and sell transactions. - No special conditions or restrictions are applied to the order. Oddlot 2 - It means the order is an odd lot type - It is used when quantity is less than the standard trading lot size - These are small or non-standard share quantities (not full lots) - It is treated separately from normal lot trading in the system.Useful for small quantity or partial share trading orders - Example: • Suppose the normal trading lot size is 100 shares • A trader places an order for 25 shares of Reliance Industries • Since 25 is less than the standard lot size (100), it is treated as an Odd Lot order • In the system/API, this order will be marked as: Oddlot = 2 RetailDebt 3 - represents a retail debt order type - It is used for buying/selling debt instruments like bonds or government securities - These trades are done by retail (individual) investors, not big institutions - It usually involves small investment amounts Auction 4 - represents orders placed in an auction market - It is used when securities are traded through a bidding process instead of normal trading - Buyers and sellers submit bids, and the best price gets matched - It is often used in special cases like exchange auctions or settlement auctions CallAuction1 5 - represents a specific call auction order type (Phase 1) - Used to find a single fair market price by matching many buy and sell orders at once. - Orders are first collected, then the system calculates one price, and finally trades are executed together in one batch. CallAuction2 6 - means a second type of call auction session where orders are not executed instantly. - Orders are first collected and then a single fair price is discovered by the system. - After price discovery, all matching buy and sell orders are executed together in one batch. - it is a batch trading mode where trades happen together at one final auction price.
docs.title: 10. MarketType

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description SingleOrderLeg 1 - means the order contains only one trading instruction (one leg). - It is a regular standalone order, not part of a multi-leg strategy. - The order is executed independently without being linked to other orders. - In simple words: one order = one action (buy or sell) on a single instrument. SpreadFirstLeg 2 - means this order is the first leg of a spread strategy. - A spread strategy consists of two or more linked orders executed together. - The first leg is the initial buy or sell order in the spread. - Example: Buy NIFTY July Futures (first leg) and Sell NIFTY August Futures (second leg). SpreadSecondLeg 3 - means this order is the second leg of a spread strategy. - It is linked to the first leg and forms part of a multi-leg trade. - Both legs work together to implement a spread trading strategy. MultilegFirstLeg 4 - means this order is the first leg of a multi-leg trading strategy. - A multi-leg strategy contains two or more linked orders that work together. - This is the starting order of the strategy, followed by additional legs. - Example: Buy a Call Option as the first leg of an options strategy. MultilegSecondLeg 5 - means this order is the second leg of a multi-leg trading strategy. - It is linked to the first leg and helps complete the overall strategy. - Multiple legs are used together to achieve a specific trading objective. MultilegThirdLeg 6 - means this order is the third leg of a multi-leg trading strategy. - It is linked with the first and second legs as part of the same strategy. - Multi-leg strategies use several connected orders to achieve a trading goal.
docs.title: 11. OrderLegStatus

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description EntryLeg 1 - indicates that this order is the entry (starting) leg of a trading strategy. - It is the first order placed to open or initiate a position before any related exit or adjustment orders. ProfitTargetExitLeg 2 - indicates that this order is used to exit a position when the desired profit target is reached. - It helps automatically close the trade and lock in profits once the specified target price is achieved. StoplossExitLeg 3 - indicates that this order is used to exit a position when the price reaches a predefined loss limit. - It helps reduce potential losses by automatically closing the trade when the stop-loss price is triggered. \

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description DAY 1 - means the order remains active only for the current trading day. - If the order is not executed by the end of the trading session, it is automatically cancelled. NET 2 - means the position is viewed and managed on a net basis, where all buy and sell trades are combined into a single net position. - Includes delivery trades (CNC) or carry-forward derivative positions (NRML). - For example, if you buy 100 shares and sell 40 shares, your net position becomes 60 shares long.

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description Futures 1 - Futures are contracts to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a future date. - They are commonly used for hedging risk or speculating on price movements. - Standardized derivative contracts to buy or sell an asset (stock, index, commodity, or currency) at a predetermined price on a future date. Options 2 - Options are contracts that give the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a specified price before expiry. - They are used for hedging and advanced trading strategies. - Derivative contracts that give the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy (Call) or sell (Put) the underlying asset at a fixed price within a specified time. Spread 4 - Spread is a trading strategy involving two or more related positions taken together. - It aims to profit from the price difference between the instruments. - A strategy involving simultaneous buying and selling of related instruments. Equity 8 - Equity represents ownership shares in a company. - Investors buy and sell equities to participate in the company's growth and returns. - Shares of listed companies traded in the cash market segment. Spot 16 - Spot refers to the immediate purchase or sale of a financial instrument at the current market price. - Settlement usually occurs within the standard exchange settlement cycle. - Trades for immediate delivery and settlement at the current market price, typically used in currencies and commodities. PreferenceShares 32 - Preference Shares are shares that provide priority in dividend payments over common equity shares. - They generally have fixed dividends but limited voting rights. - A class of shares that provides fixed dividends and has priority over equity shares in dividend distribution and liquidation, but usually with limited voting rights. Debentures 64 - Debentures are debt instruments issued by companies to raise funds from investors. - They pay fixed interest and are repaid on a specified maturity date. - Long-term debt instruments issued by companies or governments to raise funds. Typically carry fixed interest payments. Warrants 128 - Warrants are financial instruments that give the holder the right to buy a company's shares at a fixed price before a certain date. - They are often issued along with bonds or other securities. - Financial instruments that give the holder the right to buy equity shares at a specific price before a set expiry date. Miscellaneous 256 - Miscellaneous includes financial instruments that do not fall under standard categories. - It serves as a generic classification for special or uncommon instruments. - Category for instruments that do not fall into standard classifications (used for special or rare products). MutualFund 512 - Mutual Fund is an investment vehicle that pools money from multiple investors and invests in a diversified portfolio. - It is managed by professional fund managers on behalf of investors. - Units of pooled investment schemes managed by Asset Management Companies (AMCs).
docs.title: 14. InstrumentType

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description PreOpenStart 0 - Indicates the start of the Pre-Open Market session. - During this phase, traders can place, modify, or cancel orders. - No trades are executed yet. - The beginning of the pre-open session where orders can be placed but are not matched immediately. PreOpenEnd 1 - Indicates the end of the Pre-Open Market session. - The system finalizes price discovery based on collected orders. - Trading is about to move to the normal market session. - The end of the pre-open session when accumulated orders are matched and the opening price is determined. NormalStart 2 - Indicates the start of the regular trading session. - Orders are matched and executed continuously. - Normal buying and selling begins. - The start of the regular trading session where continuous matching of buy and sell orders happens. NormalEnd 4 - Indicates the end of the regular trading session. - No new trades are executed after market close. -Remaining unexecuted DAY orders are cancelled. - The close of the regular trading session; after this point, no further trades are executed in the normal market. PreClosingStart 8 - Indicates the start of the Pre-Closing session. - Used to determine the closing price of securities. - Orders may be collected for closing price calculation. - The start of the pre-closing session, where the system collects data to calculate the closing price (closing auction). PreClosingEnd 16 - Indicates the end of the Pre-Closing session. - The final closing price is determined. - Market moves toward complete closure. - The end of the pre-closing session when the official closing price is determined and published.
docs.title: 15. TradingSession

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description NONE 0 - No valuation method is applied. - The position or instrument is not valued using a specific calculation. - Used when valuation is not required. - Default flag when no special settlement type is applied. The order follows the normal market settlement rules. CL 1 - Valuation is based on the Closing Price. - The last closing market price is used for calculation. - Commonly used for end-of-day valuations. - Orders specifically placed to be executed at the market's closing price during the closing session. LT 2 - Commonly used for end-of-day valuations. - Commonly used for end-of-day valuations. - Reflects the current market value more closely. - Segment used for block deals, bulk trades, or special limited trading windows defined by the exchange.

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description T1_Holdings 1 - Shares purchased today but not yet settled. - These shares are waiting to be credited to the Demat account. - Usually become regular holdings after settlement. - Securities bought but not yet fully settled (i.e., on T+1 day). Holdings 3 - Shares that are fully settled and available in the Demat account. - Can be sold or held as a long-term investment. - Represents regular stock holdings. - Fully settled securities that are credited to the client's Demat account. MTFHoldings 3 - Shares purchased through the Margin Trading Facility (MTF). - The broker provides funding for part of the purchase value. - Investors can take larger positions using margin. Securities purchased under Margin Trading Facility where part of the funds are borrowed from the broker.

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description ParentLevel 0 - Represents the main or top-level statistics category. - Used to group related statistical data together. - Acts as the parent for one or more child levels. - Represents the top-level entity in a hierarchy. ChildLevel 1 - Represents a sub-category under a parent level. - Contains detailed statistics related to the parent category. - Used for more granular data analysis. - Represents a sub-entity under a parent.

docs.text: Enum Name Description joined - Indicates that the socket connection has been established successfully. - The client is now connected and ready to receive data. - Sent when a user joins the socket session. - Sent when a client successfully connects and joins the WebSocket channel. Confirms that the real-time stream is active. error - Indicates that an error occurred during the socket operation. - The requested action could not be completed successfully. - Usually includes error details or a message. - Indicates a failure or issue (e.g., invalid request, authentication failure, or system error). Requires client-side handling. warning - Indicates a non-critical issue or alert. - The connection is still active, but attention may be required. - Used to notify about potential problems. - Non-critical issue or advisory message (e.g., rate-limit approaching, deprecated API usage). success - Indicates that an operation completed successfully. - Confirms that the requested action was processed. - Usually returned after a successful request. - Confirms that a client request was processed successfully (e.g., order placement acknowledged). order - Indicates an order-related event. - Used to send updates about order placement or status changes. - Helps track order activity in real time. - Event carrying real-time updates about an order lifecycle — placed, modified, filled, cancelled, or rejected. trade - Indicates a trade execution event. - Sent when an order is matched and executed. - Provides trade details and execution information. - Sent when an order results in an actual trade execution (full or partial). Contains trade ID, price, and quantity details. logout - Indicates that the user has been disconnected or logged out. - The socket session is closed. - No further updates will be received until reconnection. - Notification that the session or WebSocket connection has been terminated — either manually or due to token expiry. position - Indicates a position-related update. - Sent when there is a change in the user's holdings or positions. - Helps track open positions in real time. - Real-time updates about portfolio positions, including intraday (DayWise) or carry-forward (NetWise) quantities. tradeConversion - Indicates a trade conversion event. - Sent when a trade or position is converted from one product type to another. - Example: Converting MIS to CNC. - Event triggered when an order/trade is converted from one product type to another (e.g., Intraday MIS → Delivery CNC). gttOrder - Indicates a request or response for order details. - Used to fetch information about existing orders. - Returns order-related data. - Event update for GTT Orders (orders that activate only when a trigger price is met). gttOrderRejection - Indicates an order rejection event or request. - Sent when an order is rejected by the system or exchange. - Provides the reason for rejection. - Notification when a GTT Order fails to activate due to invalid conditions, margin shortfall, or exchange rejection.
docs.title: 19. Socket Event

docs.text: Enum Name Numeric Code Description AMO 1 - AMO (After Market Order) allows orders to be placed after market hours. - The order is sent to the exchange when the market opens. - Useful when you cannot place orders during trading hours. - Standard market order placed during regular market hours. OT 2 - OT (Order Through Trading Hours) indicates a regular order placed during market hours. - The order is sent directly to the exchange for execution. - Used for normal day-to-day trading. - After Market Order — Orders placed after market hours to be processed when the market opens. INSTI 4 - INSTI indicates that the order is placed by an institutional investor. - Typically used by banks, mutual funds, or large financial institutions. - Such orders are usually larger in size than retail orders. - Institutional — Orders placed through institutional trading sessions. GTT 5 - GTT (Good Till Triggered) is an order that remains active until a specified trigger price is reached. - The order is automatically placed when the trigger condition is met. - Useful for long-term buy or sell targets. - Good Till Triggered — Order remains pending until the trigger condition is met.
docs.title: 20. Order Session Type

docs.text: GTT (Good Till Triggered) Orders A GTT Order stays saved with the broker until the market reaches a predefined trigger price . Once triggered, the order is automatically sent to the exchange — no need to monitor the market continuously. Auto trigger No monitoring needed Planned trading Price-based entry Buy & sell support Long-term investing How It Works Create GTT Order → Order Saved by Broker → Market Monitored → Trigger Hit → Order Executed Components of a GTT Order Trading Symbol The stock or instrument to trade. RELIANCE, TCS, INFY Trigger Price Market price that activates the GTT order. ₹2,750 → order fires Order Price The actual price placed at exchange after trigger. Limit ₹2,748 Quantity Number of shares or contracts. 100 Shares Examples Example 1 — Buy GTT Current price: ₹2,700 Trigger price set: ₹2,750 RELIANCE rises to ₹2,750 Buy order sent automatically Example 2 — Sell GTT You hold RELIANCE at ₹2,800 Sell trigger set: ₹2,900 RELIANCE rises to ₹2,900 Sell order sent automatically GTT Order Status Status Description Active Stored and waiting for the trigger price to be reached Triggered Trigger price reached — order has been sent to the exchange Filled Order completely executed by the exchange Partially Filled Only part of the order has been executed Cancelled GTT order cancelled by the user before being triggered Expired GTT order expired before trigger price was reached Rejected Exchange rejected the order after it was triggered GTT Order vs Normal Order NORMAL ORDER Sent to exchange immediately Active only for current trading day Requires manual placement Suitable for immediate trading → GTT ORDER Stored until trigger price is reached Stays active till triggered or expired Fires automatically at trigger price Suitable for future price-based trading Advantages & Limitations Advantages No need to monitor market continuously Automatically places orders at trigger Helps plan trades in advance Reduces emotional trading decisions Suitable for long-term investors Works for both Buy and Sell sides Limitations Order not sent to exchange until trigger Triggering does not guarantee execution May expire based on broker policy Fast market moves may leave limit unfilled Requires sufficient funds at trigger time Common Use Cases Buy at Desired Price Automatically buy a stock when it reaches a specific price. Sell at Target Automatically sell holdings when the desired price is reached. Breakout Trading Enter a trade when price breaks above or below a level. Long-Term Investing Place buy or sell orders in advance without daily monitoring. !!! tip Always ensure sufficient funds or holdings are available when the trigger fires. Review active GTT orders regularly and cancel unused ones to avoid unintended trades. Place GTT Order Places a Good Till Triggered (GTT) order that remains active until a specified trigger condition is met. Once the trigger price is reached, the system automatically places the corresponding market or limit order on the exchange. docs.text: MTM (Mark-to-Market) Calculation MTM is the profit or loss on your open position based on the current market price (LTP) . It tells you how much you would gain or lose if you closed the position right now. Real-time P&L Unrealized Profit/Loss F&O Daily Settlement Position Monitoring What is MTM? MTM (Mark-to-Market) is the real-time profit or loss of an open position, calculated using the latest market price (LTP). Since the position has not been closed yet, this is an unrealized profit or loss — it changes continuously as the market price moves. OPEN POSITION MTM updates live with each LTP change UNREALIZED No actual cash change until position closes CONTINUOUS Recalculated every tick throughout the day MTM Formula Long (Buy) Position MTM = ( LTP − Avg Buy Price ) × Quantity If LTP > Buy Price → Profit If LTP < Buy Price → Loss Short (Sell) Position MTM = ( Avg Sell Price − LTP ) × Quantity If LTP < Sell Price → Profit If LTP > Sell Price → Loss Examples Example 1 — Long Position (Profit) PROFIT Stock ABC Ltd. Quantity 100 shares Avg Buy Price ₹500 Current LTP ₹530 MTM = (530 − 500) × 100 = ₹30 × 100 MTM = +₹3,000 Profit Example 2 — Long Position (Loss) LOSS Stock ABC Ltd. Quantity 100 shares Avg Buy Price ₹500 Current LTP ₹480 MTM = (480 − 500) × 100 = −₹20 × 100 MTM = −₹2,000 Loss Example 3 — Short Position (Profit) PROFIT Stock ABC Ltd. Quantity 100 shares Avg Sell Price ₹500 Current LTP ₹470 MTM = (500 − 470) × 100 = ₹30 × 100 MTM = +₹3,000 Profit Example 4 — Short Position (Loss) LOSS Stock ABC Ltd. Quantity 100 shares Avg Sell Price ₹500 Current LTP ₹520 MTM = (500 − 520) × 100 = −₹20 × 100 MTM = −₹2,000 Loss How MTM Changes with LTP You bought 100 shares at ₹500 . Watch how MTM moves with price: Current LTP MTM Status ₹490 −₹1,000 Loss ₹500 ₹0 Break-even ₹510 +₹1,000 Profit ₹520 +₹2,000 Profit ₹540 +₹4,000 Profit MTM vs Realized P&L 📊 MTM (Mark-to-Market) Calculated on open positions Changes with every market price movement Unrealized profit or loss No cash impact until position is closed ✅ Realized P&L Calculated after position is closed Fixed once the trade is completed Actual booked profit or loss Cash is credited/debited to account Transition Example: Buy 100 shares @ ₹500 → LTP = ₹520 MTM = +₹2,000 → Sell @ ₹520 Realized = +₹2,000 | MTM = ₹0 Why MTM is Important Shows your real-time profit or loss on every open position Helps you monitor open positions and decide to hold or exit Used in F&O daily settlement by exchanges Assists in managing overall trading risk across positions Helps plan entries and exits based on current P&L Improves discipline — you always know where you stand Real-Life Example — Anita Anita buys 200 shares of XYZ Ltd. at ₹150 at market open. LTP rises to ₹160 MTM = (160 − 150) × 200 = ₹10 × 200 +₹2,000 Profit LTP falls to ₹145 MTM = (145 − 150) × 200 = −₹5 × 200 −₹1,000 Loss Anita has not sold the shares — her MTM keeps updating with every price tick. In Simple Words: MTM (Mark-to-Market) is the current profit or loss on an open position. It is calculated using the latest market price (LTP) and keeps updating as the market price changes. Once the position is closed, the MTM converts into Realized P&L. MTM Calculation MTM represents the realized and unrealized profit or loss calculated using the user's current position and the instrument's Last Traded Price (LTP). MTM values are not provided in Interactive API responses; users must compute MTM on their end using current position data that can be fetched by GET Position api or Position data received on Interactive websocket. LastTradedPrice for a particular instrument can be fetched using marketdata apis & websocket. Refer to the sample logic provided below. openBuyQty = int (position[ "OpenBuyQuantity" ]) openSellQty = int (position[ "OpenSellQuantity" ]) # Realized MTM def safe_div (numerator, denominator): return float (numerator) / float (denominator) if denominator else 0.0 if openBuyQty == 0 or openSellQty == 0 : realizedMTM = 0.0 else : totalSquaredOffQuantity = min (openBuyQty, openSellQty) sellWeightedAvgPrice = safe_div (position[ "SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceSell" ], openSellQty) buyWeightedAvgPrice = safe_div (position[ "SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceBuy" ], openBuyQty) realizedMTM = ( totalSquaredOffQuantity * (sellWeightedAvgPrice - buyWeightedAvgPrice) * ( float (position[ "Multiplier" ]) * PriceNumerator / PriceDenominator) ) # Unrealized MTM if int (position[ "Quantity" ]) > 0 : lastPrice = lastPrice if lastPrice and lastPrice != 0 else closePrice squareOfPrice = lastPrice if squareOfPrice == 0.0 : unRealizedMTM = 0.0 else : buyWeightedAvgPrice = float (position[ "SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceBuy" ]) / float (position[ "OpenBuyQuantity" ]) unRealizedMTM = abs ( int (position[ "Quantity" ])) * (squareOfPrice - buyWeightedAvgPrice) * ( float (position[ "Multiplier" ]) * PriceNumerator / PriceDenominator) else : lastPrice = lastPrice if lastPrice and lastPrice != 0 else closePrice squareOfPrice = lastPrice if squareOfPrice == 0.0 : unRealizedMTM = 0.0 else : sellWeightedAvgPrice = float (position[ "SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceSell" ]) / float (position[ "OpenSellQuantity" ]) if not sellWeightedAvgPrice or sellWeightedAvgPrice != sellWeightedAvgPrice: sellWeightedAvgPrice = 0.0 unRealizedMTM = ( abs ( int (position[ "Quantity" ])) * (sellWeightedAvgPrice - squareOfPrice) * ( float (position[ "Multiplier" ]) * PriceNumerator / PriceDenominator) ) totalMTM = realizedMTM + unRealizedMTM Copy Show Full

docs.text: Margin Calculator Estimate the margin required before placing a trade — based on exchange, product type, quantity, and price — to ensure you have sufficient funds in your account. Instant Calculation All Segments Risk Management Pre-trade Margin What is Margin? Margin is the minimum amount of funds required in your account to place or hold a trade . It acts as a security deposit to cover potential losses. The exchange sets margin requirements based on the instrument, product type, and market volatility. Simple Example — RELIANCE MIS Trade INSTRUMENT RELIANCE EXCHANGE NSECM QUANTITY 100 PRICE ₹2,850 PRODUCT MIS Estimated Required Margin ₹57,000 The calculated amount is an estimate of the funds required to place this trade successfully. Types of Margin S SPAN Margin Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk. The minimum margin required by the exchange for F&O positions, calculated based on the worst possible loss scenario. E Exposure Margin An additional buffer collected by the exchange over SPAN margin to cover mark-to-market losses and other risks not captured by SPAN. V VAR Margin Value at Risk margin applies to equity cash (CNC/MIS) positions. Computed based on the stock's historical price volatility over a defined period. E ELM Margin Extreme Loss Margin is collected to cover losses beyond VAR . It is a fixed percentage set by the exchange for each security. How Margin Calculation Works 👤 Select Instrument → ⚙️ Enter Trade Details → 🧮 Margin Calculation → 💰 Required Margin Why Margin Matters Avoid insufficient margin errors before placing orders Plan trades by knowing exact fund requirements upfront Supports Equity, F&O, Currency, and Commodity Saves time with instant pre-trade estimates Helps manage risk across multiple positions Improves overall trading discipline and planning In Simple Words: Margin is the security deposit you must have in your account before placing a trade. The Margin Calculator API lets you check this requirement instantly before submitting any order. Order Margin Details Calculate the margin required for a new order before placing it. docs.text: Rate Limiting Rate limiting controls the number of requests a client can make to an API within a specific time period — maintaining platform stability, ensuring fair usage, and protecting backend services from excessive traffic. Per-second limits 429 Too Many Requests Rate-limit headers Unified throttle Exponential backoff Fair resource allocation Why Rate Limiting Is Important Prevent Overload Stops servers from being overwhelmed during peak traffic periods. Fair Usage Ensures equal resource allocation among all users and clients. Reliability Maintains consistent API performance and platform availability. Abuse Protection Guards against accidental loops, bots, and excessive automation. How Rate Limits Work Each endpoint is assigned a maximum number of requests allowed per second (RPS) . Requests beyond the limit are rejected until the window resets. ✅ Allowed — 10 req/sec limit Request 1 → ✓ Request 2 → ✓ Request 3 → ✓ ⋮ (up to 10) Request 10 → ✓ 10 requests within 1 second — accepted ❌ Rejected — 10 req/sec limit Request 1–10 → ✓ Request 11 → ✗ 429 Request 12 → ✗ 429 Request 13 → ✗ 429 Request 14 → ✗ 429 15 requests within 1 second — 5 rejected Rate Limit Response When the rate limit is exceeded the API returns HTTP 429 : 429 Too Many Requests { "type": "error", "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", "description": "Request rate exceeded the allowed limit. Please retry after some time." } Rate Limit Headers X-RateLimit-Limit Maximum requests allowed per window X-RateLimit-Remaining Remaining requests in the current window X-RateLimit-Reset Unix timestamp when the limit resets EXAMPLE RESPONSE HEADERS X-RateLimit-Limit: 10 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3 X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718700000 Rate Limits Table API Name Endpoint Method Limit (Req/Sec) Unified Order API Throttle Limit Unified Order API Throttle Limit See Note ↓ 10 Balance /user/balance GET 1 Profile /user/profile GET 1 Brokerage Calculator /user/calculatebrokerage POST 10 Cancel All /orders/cancelall POST 1 Orderbook / Order History /orders GET 1 Tradebook /orders/trades GET 1 Spread Orderbook /orders/spread GET 1 Place GTT Order /orders/gttorder POST 1 Modify GTT Order /orders/gttorder PUT 1 Cancel GTT Order /orders/gttorder DELETE 1 GTT Orderbook /orders/gttorderbook GET 1 Holding /portfolio/holdings GET 1 Position /portfolio/positions GET 1 Position Convert /portfolio/positions/convert PUT 10 Regular Order Margin /orders/margindetails POST 10 Regular Order Modify Margin /orders/modifyordermargindetails POST 10 Cover Order Margin /orders/comargindetails POST 10 Cover Order Modify Margin /orders/comodifymargindetails POST 10 Bracket Order Margin /orders/bomargindetails POST 10 Exchange Status /status/exchange GET 1 Exchange Message /messages/exchange GET 1 Note — Unified Order Throttle Limit: This is a combined rate limit applied across all order-related APIs listed below. The standard limit is 10 requests per second , shared cumulatively among these APIs: Place Order, Modify Order, Cancel Order, Place BO (Bracket Order), Modify BO, Cancel BO, Place CO (Cover Order), Exit Cover, Place Spread Order, Modify Spread Order, Cancel Spread Order. Unified Order Throttle Limit Certain order-management APIs share a combined throttle limit — the total across all three endpoints cannot exceed 10 req/second. Unified Order APIs POST Place Order PUT Modify Order DELETE Cancel Order Shared limit: 10 requests/second Example — Limit Exceeded Place Order → 5 req Modify Order → 3 req Cancel Order → 4 req Total = 12 req/sec → Rate limit exceeded (max 10) Best Practices Exponential Backoff On 429, wait 1s → retry. If still failing, wait 2s → 4s → 8s before each retry. Cache Responses Cache frequently requested data (e.g., instruments, profile) to avoid redundant API calls. Monitor Headers Read X-RateLimit-Remaining before sending batches to stay within limits. Queue Requests Queue non-critical requests and spread them over time rather than bursting all at once. Avoid Polling Use WebSocket streaming instead of repeatedly polling REST endpoints for updates. ⏱ Respect Retry Intervals Wait the duration specified by the API in the retry response before re-sending. Notes Rate limits may vary by endpoint — always check the endpoint-specific table. Limits are subject to change to ensure platform stability. Repeated violations may result in temporary throttling or access restrictions.

docs.text: Socket Streaming Socket Streaming is a way to receive live, real-time data from the server without sending repeated requests . Once connected, the server automatically pushes new data whenever it becomes available. Real-time Data Persistent Connection Low Latency Live Trading Ready What is Socket Streaming? Socket Streaming is a real-time communication method where the server continuously pushes live data to the client over a single, always-open connection. You connect once, and the server sends updates automatically — no repeated requests needed. CONNECT ONCE Open a single persistent connection to the server SERVER PUSHES Server automatically sends updates as they happen INSTANT UPDATES Zero wait — data arrives the moment it changes Why Use Socket Streaming? Without Socket Streaming (Polling) Client → Request latest price Server → ₹250 Client → Request latest price Server → ₹251 Client → Request latest price Server → ₹249 Many API requests — even when data has not changed. With Socket Streaming Client ───────────────► Server Connect Once Server ─► ₹250 Server ─► ₹251 Server ─► ₹249 Server ─► ₹252 Server automatically pushes updates as prices change. How Socket Streaming Works Application Starts ▼ Connect to WebSocket Server ▼ Connection Established ▼ Subscribe to Required Data ▼ Server Sends Live Updates ▼ Application Updates Screen Instantly Example in a Trading Application Suppose you subscribe to ABC Ltd. The server pushes prices automatically throughout the session: Time Event Price 9:15:00 AM Market opens — first tick received ₹500 9:15:03 AM Price update pushed by server ₹501 ▲ 9:15:07 AM Price update pushed by server ₹499 ▼ 9:15:12 AM Price update pushed by server ₹503 ▲ No API requests were made after the initial connection — all updates delivered automatically. Data That Can Be Streamed Live stock prices (LTP) Market depth (Bid / Ask) OHLC (Open, High, Low, Close) Volume & market statistics Index values (NIFTY, SENSEX) Order status updates Trade confirmations Position updates Portfolio updates REST API vs Socket Streaming REST API Request → Response Client requests data from server One request returns one response Suitable for static or occasional data Requires repeated API calls for updates Higher latency for live updates Socket Streaming Connect Once → Receive Always Server pushes data automatically One connection delivers continuous updates Designed for live market data No repeated requests after connection Very low latency Advantages of Socket Streaming Real-time updates Faster than polling Lower network overhead Reduced server load Better user experience Ideal for live trading Things to Remember The connection stays open until it is closed or disconnected by either side. If the connection drops, the client should reconnect automatically . You must subscribe to specific symbols or data types after connecting. Multiple symbols can be streamed over the same single connection . Real-Life Analogy — Cricket Match REST API — Refreshing Scorecard Like refreshing a webpage every 10 seconds to see the latest cricket score. You get the score, but only when you ask — and you may miss updates in between. Socket Streaming — Live TV Like watching the match live on TV . The score updates the instant a wicket falls or a run is scored — no refresh needed, no delay. Socket Streaming in RMoney Market Data API The RMoney Market Data API uses socket streaming to deliver live market data across all subscribed instruments. LIVE QUOTES Real-time price updates for subscribed instruments MARKET DEPTH Best bid and ask prices with available quantities OHLC UPDATES Open, High, Low, and Close prices streamed live VOLUME Total traded volume and other market statistics INDEX UPDATES Live values of NIFTY, SENSEX, and other indices MULTI-SYMBOL Stream multiple instruments over one connection Typical Flow Connect to WebSocket ▼ Authenticate (if required) ▼ Subscribe to Instruments ▼ Receive Live Market Data ▼ Unsubscribe or Disconnect In Simple Words: Socket Streaming lets your application receive live updates over a single, continuous connection. Once connected, the server automatically sends new market data — such as prices, orders, or positions — as soon as it changes, making it ideal for real-time trading applications. Establishment of socket connection import socketio url = "https://developers.symphonyfintech.in" # base url userID = "RM" #userID received from login api token = "xxxxxx" #Token generated from login api apiType = "INTERACTIVE" socketio_path = "/1interactive/socket.io" #note:- /1interactive is endpoint you have recieved from hostlookup load balance step logger = False # or "True" sio = socketio. Client () if __name__ == "__main__" : try : connectionString = f"{url}?token={token}&userID={userID}&apiType={apiType}" sio . connect (url=connectionString, socketio_path=socketio_path, transports=[ "websocket" ]) sio . wait () except KeyboardInterrupt: print ( "Stopping client..." ) sio . disconnect () except Exception as e: print ( "Connection failed:" , e) Copy Show Full Note: XTS uses Socket.io protocol for the Interactive order related data. Users must note that some programming languages does not support socket.io protocol directly, so they need to find compatible websocket libraries. Connect This event triggers when socket connection is successfull. @sio. on ( "connect" ) def connect (): print ( "Connection Established" ) Copy Joined If a successful connection is established with the server, this event will be raised to indicate that the user has been connected. @sio. on ( "joined" ) def on_joined (data): print ( "Socket Joined" , data) Copy Error In case of any error with the server, this event will be raised along with the cause of the error. For example, if you send an incorrect token while connecting, the server will raise this event and disconnect your socket connection. @sio. on ( "error" ) def on_error (data): print ( "Error" , data) Copy Disconnect In case a socket disconnection occurs with the server, this event will be raised to indicate the disconnection. @sio. on ( "disconnect" ) def on_disconnect (): print ( "Disconnected" ) Copy Orders To listen for order state change events such as New, Filled, Partially Filled, etc., register for this event. @sio. on ( "order" ) def on_order (data): print ( "Order Received:- " ,data) Copy Below is order object you will receive when any of your order state changes { "LoginID" : "RM1" , "ClientID" : "RM1" , "AppOrderID" : 648468730 , "OrderReferenceID" : "" , "GeneratedBy" : "WSAPI" , "ExchangeOrderID" : "1005239196374100" , "OrderCategoryType" : "NORMAL" , "ExchangeSegment" : "NSECM" , "ExchangeInstrumentID" : 16921 , "OrderSide" : "BUY" , "OrderType" : "LIMIT" , "ProductType" : "NRML" , "TimeInForce" : "DAY" , "OrderPrice" : 0 , "OrderQuantity" : 1 , "OrderStatus" : "New" , "OrderAverageTradedPrice" : 2615.8 , "LeavesQuantity" : 1 , "CumulativeQuantity" : 0 , "OrderDisclosedQuantity" : 0 , "OrderGeneratedDateTime" : "14-05-2021 11:17:29" , "ExchangeTransactTime" : "14-05-2021 11:17:30" , "LastUpdateDateTime" : "14-05-2021 11:17:29" , "OrderExpiryDate" : "01-01-1900 00:00:00" , "CancelRejectReason" : "" , "OrderUniqueIdentifier" : "454845" , "OrderLegStatus" : "SingleOrderLeg" , "IsSpread" : false , "BolegDetails" : "" , "MessageCode" : 4 , "MessageVersion" : 4 , "ApplicationType" : 0 , "SequenceNumber" : 0 } Copy Show Full Trade When any order gets executed (fully or partially filled), a new trade event will be generated. The server will raise trade events, and you can listen to these events by registering for them. @sio. on ( "trade" ) def on_trade (data): print ( "Trade Recieved:- " , data) Copy Below is trade object you will receive when any trade happens on your account. { "LoginID" : "YMS" , "ClientID" : "YMSCL1" , "AppOrderID" : 648468731 , "OrderReferenceID" : "" , "GeneratedBy" : "TWSAPI" , "ExchangeOrderID" : "1005239196374109" , "OrderCategoryType" : "NORMAL" , "ExchangeSegment" : "NSECM" , "ExchangeInstrumentID" : 16921 , "OrderSide" : "BUY" , "OrderType" : "Limit" , "ProductType" : "NRML" , "TimeInForce" : "DAY" , "OrderPrice" : 0 , "OrderQuantity" : 1 , "OrderStatus" : "Filled" , "OrderAverageTradedPrice" : 44.00 , "LeavesQuantity" : 0 , "CumulativeQuantity" : 1 , "OrderDisclosedQuantity" : 0 , "OrderGeneratedDateTime" : "14-05-2021 11:17:29" , "ExchangeTransactTime" : "14-05-2021 11:17:30" , "LastUpdateDateTime" : "14-05-2021 11:17:29" , "OrderUniqueIdentifier" : "454845" , "OrderLegStatus" : "SingleOrderLeg" , "LastTradedPrice" : 44 , "LastTradedQuantity" : 1 , "LastExecutionTransactTime" : "14-05-2021 11:17:29" , "ExecutionID" : "1320599156383056" , "ExecutionReportIndex" : 3 , "IsSpread" : false , "MessageCode" : 9005 , "MessageVersion" : 4 , "TokenID" : 0 , "ApplicationType" : 0 , "SequenceNumber" : 0 } Copy Show Full Position If any position change occurs in your account, the server will raise this event to indicate the updated position. By registering for this event, you can track position changes. @sio. on ( "position" ) def on_position (data): print ( "Position Recieved:- " , data) Copy Below is Position object that you will receive when any position change happens on your account. { "LoginID" : "RM1" , "AccountID" : "RM1" , "TradingSymbol" : "ACC" , "ExchangeSegment" : "NSECM" , "ExchangeInstrumentID" : "22" , "ProductType" : "CNC" , "Multiplier" : 1 , "MarketLot" : 1 , "BuyAveragePrice" : 41.78 , "SellAveragePrice" : 41.63 , "LongPosition" : 5 , "ShortPosition" : 0 , "NetPosition" : 5 , "BuyValue" : 1671.00 , "SellValue" : 2498.00 , "NetValue" : 827.00 , "UnrealizedMTM" : 0 , "RealizedMTM" : 0 , "MTM" : 0 , "BEP" : 0 , "SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceBuy" : 1671.00 , "SumOfTradedQuantityAndPriceSell" : 2498.00 , "StatisticsLevel" : "ParentLevel" , "IsInterOpPosition" : false , "childPositions" : [{}], "MessageCode" : 9002 , "MessageVersion" : 1 , "TokenID" : 0 , "ApplicationType" : 0 , "SequenceNumber" : 0 } Copy Show Full Trade conversion If any trade conversion occurs in your account, the server will raise this event to indicate the trade conversion status. docs.text: Spread Orders A Spread Order places two related positions (legs) simultaneously — one buy and one sell — to profit from the price difference between two instruments rather than the movement of a single one. Two-leg order Reduced market risk Simultaneous execution Price spread trading F&O strategies Efficient execution Two Legs of a Spread Order BUY LEG Buy Leg The instrument you want to buy. Buy NIFTY July Future ⇄ SELL LEG Sell Leg The related instrument you want to sell. Sell NIFTY August Future How It Works Create Spread Order → Select Buy Leg → Select Sell Leg → Sent to Exchange → Both Legs Executed Example — NIFTY Calendar Spread Leg Action Instrument Buy Leg BUY NIFTY July Future Sell Leg SELL NIFTY August Future If the price difference (spread) between July and August contracts changes in your favor, you make a profit — even if the overall market moves only slightly. Spread Order vs Normal Order NORMAL ORDER Single buy or sell order Trades one instrument Higher market exposure Regular equity & derivative trading → SPREAD ORDER Two linked orders (buy + sell) Trades price difference between two instruments Lower market risk Futures & options strategies Advantages & Limitations Advantages Reduces overall market risk Both legs executed together Suitable for F&O strategies Profit from price differences No need for multiple separate orders Limitations Supported on select exchanges only Both instruments must be related More complex than a regular order Requires spread strategy knowledge Common Use Cases 📅 Calendar Spread Buy one month's futures and sell another month's futures contract. 🏭 Commodity Spread Trade the price difference between two related commodity contracts. 📊 Options Spread Combine multiple option contracts to manage risk and potential profit. ⚖️ Arbitrage Trading Take advantage of price differences between related instruments or markets. !!! tip Always choose related instruments, ensure sufficient margin for both positions, and verify exchange support before placing a Spread Order. docs.text: Base URL & Endpoints Before making any API request, you need to know where the API lives and which path to call . This page explains the building blocks of every RMoney API call. Base URL Main server address + Endpoint Specific resource path = Full API URL Complete request address What is a Base URL? Base URL The main address of the API server. Every request starts here — think of it as the building's street address. Interactive API https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 Market Data API https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 Endpoint A specific path that accesses a particular resource or action. Think of it as the room number inside the building. Login — Interactive /interactive/user/session Login — Market Data /apimarketdata/auth/login Place Order /interactive/orders URL Structure https:// Protocol xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 Domain + Port /interactive/orders Endpoint Available API Categories Authentication /interactive/user/session Orders /interactive/orders Portfolio /interactive/portfolio Funds /interactive/user/balance Market Data /apimarketdata/instruments WebSocket ws://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 Authentication Endpoints Method Endpoint Description POST /interactive/user/session Interactive login — get trading token DELETE /interactive/user/session Interactive logout POST /apimarketdata/auth/login Market Data login — get market token DELETE /apimarketdata/auth/logout Market Data logout Market Data Endpoints Method Endpoint Description POST /apimarketdata/instruments/quotes Get live quotes POST /apimarketdata/instruments/master Full instrument list POST /apimarketdata/instruments/ohlc Historical OHLC candles GET /apimarketdata/instruments/search Search instruments by name Orders Endpoints Method Endpoint Description GET /interactive/orders Get order book POST /interactive/orders Place new order PUT /interactive/orders Modify existing order DELETE /interactive/orders Cancel order GET /interactive/orders/trades Get trade book Portfolio Endpoints Method Endpoint Description GET /interactive/portfolio/holdings Demat holdings GET /interactive/portfolio/positions Open positions POST /interactive/user/balance Account funds and margin PUT /interactive/portfolio/positions Convert position product type HTTP Methods Explained GET Retrieve Data Fetch existing resources without changing anything. GET /interactive/orders POST Create Resource Send data to create a new resource or trigger an action. POST /interactive/orders PUT Update Resource Modify an existing resource with new values. PUT /interactive/orders DELETE Remove Resource Delete or cancel an existing resource. DELETE /interactive/orders Sample Request and Response Request GET /interactive/orders Host: xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 Authorization: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs... Content-Type: application/json Response { "type": "success", "result": [ { "AppOrderID": 1234567890, "TradingSymbol": "RELIANCE", "OrderSide": "BUY", "OrderQuantity": 10, "OrderStatus": "Open" } ] } Best Practices Always Use HTTPS Never use plain HTTP. HTTPS encrypts all data in transit including your access token. Include Authorization Header Every protected endpoint requires your session token in the Authorization header. Validate Responses Always check the type field — even a 200 OK can contain a business-logic error. Handle Rate Limits Add delays between bulk requests. Avoid hammering endpoints — use WebSocket for live data instead. Handle Error Codes Map all HTTP status codes (401, 429, 500, etc.) to appropriate retry or alert logic in your app. Store Base URL in Config Never hardcode the base URL. Store it in environment variables so switching environments is instant. Common Response Codes 200 OK Request succeeded 201 Created Resource was created 400 Bad Request Invalid parameters in request 401 Unauthorized Missing or invalid token 403 Forbidden Token valid but access denied 404 Not Found Endpoint or resource not found 429 Too Many Requests Rate limit exceeded 500 Server Error Unexpected server-side failure Summary Base URL + Endpoint = Full API URL https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 + /interactive/orders = https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/orders Term Meaning Example Base URL Main API server address https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 Endpoint Specific resource path /interactive/orders Full URL Base URL + Endpoint https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/orders HTTP Method Action to perform GET , POST , PUT , DELETE

docs.text: Error Codes When an API request fails, RMoney returns an error code with a message so you can identify the problem and fix it fast. Understanding error codes is essential to building reliable trading applications. Identify problems quickly without guessing Debug API requests with precise context Handle failures gracefully in your application Improve overall application reliability How Errors Work Your Application API Request RMoney API Success Response Data Failure Error Code + Message Error Response Format Every error response from the RMoney API follows this consistent structure: { "type": "error", "code": "InvalidInput", "description": "Quantity must be greater than zero", "result": {} } type Always "error" when the request fails code Short machine-readable error identifier description Human-readable explanation of the error result Empty object on failure 2xx — Success Responses 2xx Request completed successfully These are not errors — they confirm everything went right. 200 OK Request completed. Data is in the response. { "type": "success", "result": { ... } } 201 Created Resource was created (e.g. order placed). { "type": "success", "result": { "AppOrderID": 1234 } } 204 No Content Successful but no response body (e.g. logout). HTTP 204 — empty body 4xx — Client Errors 4xx Problem with your request Fix the request before retrying — these errors won't resolve on their own. 400 Bad Request The API cannot understand the request due to invalid or missing data. Missing required fields Invalid parameter format Incorrect data types { "type": "error", "code": "InvalidInput", "description": "Invalid Request Parameters" } 401 Unauthorized Authentication failed. The request has no valid access token. Missing Authorization header Invalid token value Token has expired { "type": "error", "code": "Unauthorized", "description": "Unauthorized Access" } 403 Forbidden Token is valid but you don't have permission for this resource. Account not enabled for F&O Segment access not granted { "type": "error", "code": "Forbidden", "description": "Access Denied" } 404 Not Found The requested endpoint or resource does not exist. Typo in the endpoint path Order ID does not exist { "type": "error", "code": "NotFound", "description": "Resource Not Found" } 405 Method Not Allowed The HTTP method used is not supported for this endpoint. Used POST on a GET-only endpoint Wrong HTTP verb in the request { "type": "error", "code": "MethodNotAllowed", "description": "Method Not Allowed" } 429 Too Many Requests You have exceeded the allowed number of API calls per second or minute. Sending requests in a tight loop Polling instead of using WebSocket { "type": "error", "code": "RateLimitExceeded", "description": "Too Many Requests" } 5xx — Server Errors 5xx Problem on the server side Not caused by your request. Retry with exponential backoff — usually temporary. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected failure inside the API server. { "description": "Internal Server Error" } 502 Bad Gateway Server received an invalid response from an upstream service. { "description": "Bad Gateway" } 503 Service Unavailable API is down for maintenance or overloaded. Retry later. { "description": "Service Temporarily Unavailable" } 504 Gateway Timeout Server took too long to respond. Retry with a smaller request. { "description": "Gateway Timeout" } Common Trading API Errors Insufficient Funds Not enough balance or margin to place the order. { "description": "Insufficient Funds" } Invalid Symbol Trading symbol not found in the exchange segment. { "description": "Symbol Not Found" } Market Closed Request sent outside trading hours. Exchange is closed. { "description": "Market is Closed" } Invalid Quantity Order quantity is zero, negative, or not a valid lot size. { "description": "Invalid Quantity" } Order Rejected Exchange or RMS rejected the order after it was sent. { "description": "Order Rejected by Exchange" } Token Expired Login session expired. Re-authenticate to continue. { "description": "Access Token Expired" } Error Handling Best Practices Validate Inputs Before Calling Check all required fields, types, and quantity values before sending the request. A 400 error means the problem is in your request, not the server. Required fields are present Quantities are positive integers Exchange segment codes are valid Handle 401 Proactively Don't wait for a 401 response. Track your token's issue time and refresh it before the 24-hour window expires. Receive 401 Unauthorized Use Refresh Token to re-authenticate Retry original request with new token Retry Temporary Failures with Backoff Server errors (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) are usually temporary. Use exponential backoff to avoid overwhelming the server. Retry 1 1 second Retry 2 2 seconds Retry 3 4 seconds Give up Alert user Error Code Summary 2xx Success 200 OK — request completed 201 Created — resource was made 204 No Content — success, no body 4xx Client Errors 400 Bad Request — fix your input 401 Unauthorized — re-authenticate 403 Forbidden — access denied 404 Not Found — wrong endpoint or ID 405 Method Not Allowed — wrong HTTP verb 429 Rate Limited — slow down requests 5xx Server Errors 500 Server Error — retry with backoff 502 Bad Gateway — retry 503 Unavailable — wait and retry 504 Timeout — retry smaller request

docs.text: Cancel Order API Stop a pending or open order before the exchange executes it. Send the Order ID — the broker cancels it and releases your blocked margin back to your account. Endpoint DELETE https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/orders Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description AppOrderID AppOrderID Y Unique order ID OrderUniqueIdentifier OrderUniqueIdentifier Y Echo back to identify order ClientID ClientID N ClientID which is send in request body Response Body JSON { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-user-0001" , "description" : "Request sent" , "result" : [ { "AppOrderID" : 1200043151 , "ClientID" : "RM" } ] } Copy Code Examples CURL Python curl --location --request DELETE 'https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/orders' \ --header 'Authorization: xxxxxxxxxx' \ --data ''appOrderID': int(apOrpderID), 'orderUniqueIdentifier': orderUniqueIdentifier' import requests url = "https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/orders" params = { "appOrderID" : "1000125345" "" } headers = { "orderUniqueIdentifier" : "orderUniqueIdentifier" } response = await self. _delete (' order.cancel , params) return self. _handle_response ( response, "Cancel Order" ) Copy function coShowCode(lang, btn) { ['curl','python'].forEach(function(l) { document.getElementById('co-code-' + l).style.display = 'none'; document.getElementById('co-tab-' + l).style.background = '#374151'; }); document.getElementById('co-code-' + lang).style.display = 'block'; btn.style.background = 'linear-gradient(135deg,#ff7b00,#ff9500)'; } Basic Workflow User ↓ Cancel Order API ↓ Broker Server ↓ Stock Exchange ↓ ✅ Order Cancelled Which Orders Can Be Cancelled? Open Order BUY RELIANCE @ ₹2850 — Status: Open Order is live in the exchange order book. Can be cancelled. Pending / New Order SELL TCS @ ₹4200 — Status: New Order just placed, not yet matched. Can be cancelled. Completely Filled Order BUY INFY @ ₹1600 — Status: Filled Trade already executed. Cannot be cancelled. Already Cancelled Order Status: Cancelled Order already cancelled. Duplicate request rejected. Common Use Cases Wrong Order Placement Accidentally placed 100 shares instead of 10? Cancel the order immediately before it executes. Market Conditions Changed Stock price is moving against your expectation. Cancel the pending order and avoid unwanted trades. Better Price Available Cancel the existing limit order and place a new one at a better price to improve your entry. Risk Management Remove unwanted pending orders during highly volatile sessions to control exposure. Partial Fill Scenario Original Order BUY 100 Shares of RELIANCE Status = Partially Filled Executed = 60 Shares Remaining = 40 Shares After Cancel Request Executed 60 shares → Remain valid Remaining 40 shares → Cancelled Final Status: Partially Filled → Cancelled Margin for 40 shares released back When you cancel a partially filled order, only the remaining unfilled quantity is cancelled. The already-executed shares are locked and cannot be undone. Order Life Cycle Successful Cancellation New ↓ Open ↓ Cancel Request ↓ Cancelled Already Executed New ↓ Open ↓ Filled ↓ Cancel Rejected Partial Fill Cancel New ↓ Open ↓ Partially Filled ↓ Partial → Cancelled Advanced Concepts Exchange Validation Before cancelling, the exchange checks the current order status, whether it has already been matched, and whether cancellation is allowed for that order type. Risk Management System Broker systems verify user permissions, order ownership, and any exchange-level restrictions before forwarding the cancel request. Margin Release After successful cancellation, the funds or margins that were blocked for the order are released back to the user's available balance. Race Condition If the order executes at the exact same moment as your cancel request, the cancel may be rejected and the trade will have gone through. Always check the final status. Complete Cancel Order Flow User ↓ Cancel Order API ↓ Broker Risk Management ↓ Order Management System (OMS) ↓ Exchange ↓ Order Removed from Book ↓ Margin Released ↓ Confirmation Returned In Simple Words: Cancel Order API allows users to stop a pending or open order before it gets executed. It helps traders avoid unwanted trades, manage risk, and adjust to changing market conditions — and releases blocked funds back to the account instantly. .co-status-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)); gap: 14px; margin: 16px 0; } .co-can-card { background: #f0fdf4; border: 1.5px solid #86efac; border-radius: 10px; padding: 16px; text-align: center; } .co-can-icon { font-size: 24px; margin-bottom: 6px; } .co-can-label { font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; color: #15803d; margin-bottom: 6px; } .co-can-example { font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.05); padding: 5px 10px; border-radius: 5px; margin-bottom: 6px; } .co-can-note { font-size: 12px; color: #374151; } .co-cannot-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1.5px solid #fdba74; border-radius: 10px; padding: 16px; text-align: center; } .co-cannot-icon { font-size: 24px; margin-bottom: 6px; } .co-cannot-label { font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; color: #9a3412; margin-bottom: 6px; } .co-cannot-example { font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.05); padding: 5px 10px; border-radius: 5px; margin-bottom: 6px; } .co-cannot-note { font-size: 12px; color: #374151; }

docs.text: Cancel All Orders Cancel All Orders cancels all your active (open or pending) orders at once with a single request — no need to cancel each order individually. Especially useful during volatile markets or when exiting all positions quickly. Single request Risk reduction Saves time Volatile markets Multi-order mgmt End of session Endpoint POST https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/orders/cancelall Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment Y ExchangeSegment exchangeInstrumentID ExchangeInstrumentID Y Exchange Scrip code or Symbol Token is unique identifier clientID ClientID N Client ID Mandatory in case of Dealer Request Body JSON [ { "exchangeSegment" : "NSECM" , "exchangeInstrumentID" : 3045 } ] Copy Response Body JSON { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-cancelall-0001" , "description" : "Cancel All Order Request Send Successfully" , "result" : "" } Copy Code Examples CURL Python curl --location 'https://xts.rmoneyindia.coin:3000/interactive/orders/cancelall' \ --header 'Authorization: xxxxxxxxxx' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"exchangeSegment":"NSECM","exchangeInstrumentID":"1333"}' import requests url = "https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/orders/cancelall" headers = { "Authorization" : "xxxxxxxxxx" , "Content-Type" : "application/json" } payload = { "exchangeSegment" : "NSECM" , "exchangeInstrumentID" : "1333" } response = await self. _post ( 'order.cancelall' , json .dumps ( params ) ) return self. _handle_response ( response , "Cancel All Order" ) Copy function caoShowCode(lang, btn) { ['curl','python'].forEach(function(l) { document.getElementById('cao-code-' + l).style.display = 'none'; document.getElementById('cao-tab-' + l).style.background = '#374151'; }); document.getElementById('cao-code-' + lang).style.display = 'block'; btn.style.background = 'linear-gradient(135deg,#ff7b00,#ff9500)'; } How It Works User Sends Request → Broker Finds Active Orders → Cancel Requests Sent → Exchange Processes → Status Updated Which Orders Are Affected? Can Be Cancelled Open Orders Pending / New Orders Pending Trigger Orders Partially Filled (remaining qty) Cannot Be Cancelled Fully Filled Orders Already Cancelled Orders Rejected Orders Expired Orders Example Order ID Symbol Before After Cancel All 1001 RELIANCE Open Cancelled 1002 TCS Open Cancelled 1003 INFY Pending New Cancelled 1004 HDFC Filled Filled (No Change) Cancel All Orders vs Cancel Order CANCEL ORDER Cancels one specific order Requires individual Order ID Best for single order removal → CANCEL ALL ORDERS Cancels all active orders at once No need to specify Order IDs Best for fast exits & risk control Advantages & Limitations Advantages Cancel multiple orders instantly Saves time in busy sessions Reduces market exposure quickly Prevents accidental executions Easier order management Limitations Filled orders cannot be cancelled Orders mid-execution may still fill Depends on exchange acceptance Cannot undo after execution Common Use Cases Market Volatility Cancel all pending orders during sudden market movements to avoid unwanted fills. End of Session Remove all unexecuted orders before the market closes. Strategy Change Cancel all existing orders before placing new ones with updated strategy. Risk Management Quickly reduce exposure by cancelling all pending orders at once. !!! warning Review your active orders before using Cancel All Orders. Orders already being executed may still get filled before the cancellation is processed. Use carefully during live trading.
