'linear-gradient(135deg,#ff7b00,#ff9500)'; } Basic Workflow User ↓ Place Order API ↓ Broker Server ↓ Stock Exchange ↓ Order Confirmation Order Sides BUY Purchase shares from the market. BUY 10 shares of RELIANCE Money decreases → Shares added to holdings SELL Sell shares back to the market. SELL 5 shares of RELIANCE Shares decrease → Money credited to account Order Types MARKET Executes immediately at current market price. Price may vary slightly due to market fluctuation. Use when: Speed matters more than exact price BUY 10 RELIANCE (Market) → executed at ₹2849.80 or ₹2850.10 LIMIT Executes only at your specified price . Order waits until price is reached. Use when: Price matters more than speed BUY RELIANCE @ ₹2840 → waits until price drops to ₹2840 STOP LOSS Activates a sell order automatically when price drops to your trigger price . Limits your loss. Use when: Protecting against sudden price drops Bought at ₹2850 → Trigger ₹2800 → auto-sells if price falls Product Types MIS Margin Intraday Square-off Position must be closed on the same day . Buy at 10 AM → Sell before market closes CNC Cash and Carry Delivery trading. Shares stay in your Demat account . Buy today → Hold for months or years NRML Normal Carry forward position. Used mostly in Futures & Options . F&O positions carried overnight Time In Force DAY Order remains valid for the current trading day . Cancelled at end of session if unfilled. IOC Immediate Or Cancel. Execute instantly. Any unexecuted portion is cancelled immediately. Order Life Cycle Normal Flow New ↓ Open ↓ Partially Filled ↓ Filled Rejected New ↓ Rejected Cancelled New ↓ Cancelled Advanced Concepts Partial Fill Place BUY 100 shares → only 60 available → 60 executed, 40 pending. Status: Partially Filled Slippage Expected ₹2850 but executed at ₹2850.30. The ₹0.30 difference is slippage — common with Market orders. Margin Check Before order is sent, broker checks: available funds, margin requirement, risk limits, and user permissions. Complete Order Flow User ↓ Place Order API ↓ Broker Risk Management ↓ Order Management System (OMS) ↓ Exchange ↓ Order Matching Engine ↓ Trade Execution ↓ Trade Confirmation ↓ Portfolio Update In Simple Words: Place Order API is the bridge between the user and the stock exchange. It receives buy or sell instructions, validates them, sends them to the exchange, and returns the order status back to the user.

docs.text: Funds Overview Funds represent the money available in your trading account . They determine buying power, margin utilisation, and whether you can place new orders. Trading Wallet = Funds Credit Limit = Margin Available Blocked Amount = Pending Orders What are Funds? Funds are like the wallet of your trading account . They show how much money you have, how much is being used, and how much is still free for trading. Without sufficient funds, orders cannot be placed. Real-Life Example Total ₹1,00,000 In Stocks ₹20,000 Blocked ₹10,000 Free ₹70,000 ↔ Funds API Returns Cash Balance Total deposited Used Margin Blocked for trades Available Ready to trade Buying Power With leverage Why are Funds Important? Know how much money is available for trading Manage risk and prevent overtrading Understand margin utilisation at a glance Monitor deposits and withdrawals Check buying power before placing orders Track blocked and available amounts in real time How Funds Flow User Deposits Money ↓ Funds Become Available ↓ User Places Orders ↓ Margin Gets Blocked ↓ Trades Execute ↓ ✅ Funds Updated with P&L Fund Components AVAILABLE BALANCE Amount currently free for placing new orders. ₹1,00,000 − ₹20,000 used = ₹80,000 available UTILISED MARGIN Amount blocked by open positions and pending orders. Order requires ₹15,000 → ₹15,000 gets blocked CASH BALANCE Actual money deposited via bank transfers, profits, or withdrawals. Bank transfer → Trading account → Cash balance BUYING POWER Total trading capacity including broker-provided leverage. ₹50,000 × 5× margin = ₹2,50,000 buying power BLOCKED FUNDS Amounts reserved for pending orders, margin, and fees — released when order executes or cancels. Buy 100 @ ₹100 → ₹10,000 blocked until fill/cancel PAY-IN / PAY-OUT Pay-In is money added today. Pay-Out is money withdrawn today. Deposit ₹25,000 ↑ | Withdraw ₹10,000 ↓ How P&L Affects Funds Profit Adds to Funds Bought @ ₹100 Sold @ ₹120 Profit = ₹20 per share → ₹20 gets ADDED to available balance Loss Reduces Funds Bought @ ₹100 Sold @ ₹85 Loss = ₹15 per share → ₹15 gets DEDUCTED from available balance API Endpoint ENDPOINT GET https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 /interactive/user/balance Requires: valid Authorization token Copy URL API Response Fields Field Description Example cashAvailable Free cash in the trading account ₹50,000 utilisedAmount Margin blocked by open orders/positions ₹12,500 netAvailableMargin Cash + collateral − used margin ₹52,500 collateralValue Value of pledged securities as margin ₹15,000 payin Money added to account today ₹0 payout Money withdrawn today ₹0 What Happens Internally? 1 User requests fund details — API call with valid session token 2 Session validation — broker server verifies auth token 3 Ledger data retrieved — cash balance, deposits, withdrawals fetched 4 Margin engine calculates usage — sums all blocked amounts from open orders and positions 5 Account balances updated — net available margin computed 6 Response returned — full structured JSON with all fund fields Advanced Concepts Margin Leverage Broker provides extra trading capacity. With 5× leverage, ₹20,000 capital can trade ₹1,00,000 worth of positions. Realized P&L Profit from closed trades is added to available funds immediately after the trade settles. Unrealized P&L Floating profit/loss on open positions. Not yet in funds — becomes real only when position is closed. Risk Monitoring Broker systems continuously check margin, exposure, and losses. Orders are rejected if funds fall below required margin. Common Use Cases Before Placing Orders Always check available balance before placing large orders to avoid rejection due to insufficient margin. Risk Management Monitor margin utilisation and set alerts when available balance falls below a safe threshold. Withdrawals Use Pay-Out field to know the withdrawable balance without disturbing active positions. Margin Trading Track leveraged positions — ensure enough buffer so broker does not square off positions automatically. In Simple Words: Funds represent the money available in a trading account. They determine how much a user can trade, how much margin is used, and how much remains available. The Funds API provides a complete view of cash balance, margin, blocked amounts, and buying power — helping users manage their trading efficiently. Think of Funds as the wallet of your trading account , where money flows in and out as trades execute.

docs.text: Holdings Holdings are the stocks or securities that belong to you and are stored in your demat/investment account. These are your long-term investments and remain until you sell them. Demat Account Stocks Live P&L Tracking Delivery Only Long-term Investment What are Holdings? Holdings represent the shares that you own in your Demat account after successful delivery . Unlike positions, holdings do not include intraday trades — they only show shares that have been settled and delivered to your Demat account. How Holdings Work When you buy shares for delivery (CNC) , the shares are credited to your Demat account on the settlement day. Once credited, they appear in your Holdings and you can: Days Hold for a few days Months Hold for several months Years Hold for many years There is no requirement to sell them on the same day — unlike intraday positions. Examples EXAMPLE 1 Buying Delivery Shares Buy 100 shares of ABC Ltd. at ₹500 (CNC/Delivery) 100 × ₹500 = ₹50,000 Stock Qty Avg Price ABC Ltd. 100 ₹500 EXAMPLE 2 Selling Some Shares You own 100 shares . You sell 30 shares . −30 Sold 70 Remain Stock Qty ABC Ltd. 70 EXAMPLE 3 Multiple Purchases Buy 50 @ ₹500 + Buy 50 @ ₹520 (50×500 + 50×520) ÷ 100 = ₹510 Stock Qty Avg Price ABC Ltd. 100 ₹510 Information Available in Holdings Field Description Symbol Stock name or trading symbol ISIN Unique identification number assigned to the security Exchange Exchange where the stock is traded (NSE / BSE) Quantity Total shares currently owned AvailableQuantity Shares that can be sold immediately AveragePrice Average purchase price per share LTP Last Traded Price — current market price of the stock MarketValue Current value of your holdings (Quantity × LTP) InvestedValue Total amount invested (Quantity × Average Price) UnrealizedPnL Profit or loss if you sold the shares at the current market price DayChange Today's gain or loss based on today's market movement Understanding Key Fields Quantity Number of shares you own. Reliance Industries Quantity = 50 shares owned Average Price Average price at which you bought the shares. Buy 20 @ ₹100 + Buy 30 @ ₹120 (20×100 + 30×120) ÷ 50 = ₹112 Market Value Current worth of your holdings. Market Value = Qty × LTP 100 × ₹550 = ₹55,000 Invested Value Total money spent to purchase the shares. Invested Value = Qty × Avg Price 100 × ₹500 = ₹50,000 Unrealized P&L Profit or loss if you sold now. Called unrealized because you haven't sold yet. P&L = Market Value − Invested Value ₹55,000 − ₹50,000 = +₹5,000 profit ₹48,000 − ₹50,000 = −₹2,000 loss Day Change Gain or loss during the current trading day. Yesterday close: ₹540 → Today LTP: ₹550 Day Change = +₹10 × 100 shares = +₹1,000 Lifecycle of Holdings Buy Delivery Shares ↓ Order Executed ↓ Settlement Completed ↓ Shares Credited to Demat ↓ Appear in Holdings ↓ Keep or Sell Anytime Holdings vs Positions HOLDINGS ▸ Shows stocks owned in the Demat account ▸ Only delivery shares are displayed ▸ Shares remain until sold ▸ Used mainly for investing ▸ Cannot have a negative quantity POSITIONS ▸ Shows active trading positions ▸ Includes intraday, delivery, futures, options ▸ May close on the same day or remain open ▸ Used for tracking trading activity ▸ Can be long (positive) or short (negative) Real-Life Example You buy 100 shares of XYZ Ltd. at ₹200 for delivery. A few months later, the stock rises to ₹260 . Field Value Quantity 100 AveragePrice ₹200 LTP ₹260 InvestedValue ₹20,000 MarketValue ₹26,000 UnrealizedProfit +₹6,000 If you later sell all 100 shares, the holdings for XYZ Ltd. become 0 , and the profit becomes realized . Why Holdings Are Important Track the stocks you currently own Monitor current value of your investments View unrealized profit or loss Decide when to buy more or sell Build a long-term investment portfolio In Simple Words: Holdings are the delivery shares that you own in your Demat account. They show what stocks you currently own, how much you invested, their current market value, and whether you are in profit or loss. docs.text: Portfolio Overview Get a complete picture of your account — what you own , what positions you hold, and how your investments are performing in real time. Digital Folder = Portfolio Bank Statement = Holdings API Report Card = P&L Summary What is a Portfolio? A portfolio is a digital folder that holds all the stocks, mutual funds, bonds, and other securities owned by an investor. Just like a bank statement shows your money, the portfolio shows all your investments in one place. Real-Life Example 20 shares Reliance Industries 10 shares TCS 50 shares HDFC Bank Together = Your Portfolio ↔ What Portfolio API Gives Holdings Stocks you own Positions Active open trades Market Value Current worth P&L Profit or Loss Why is Portfolio Important? Track all investments in one place Monitor profit and loss in real time Understand current holdings and their value Measure overall investment performance Make better, data-driven decisions Diversify risk across different assets Portfolio Workflow User Makes API Request ↓ Broker Server ↓ Account Database ↓ Holdings & Positions Retrieved ↓ P&L Calculated ↓ ✅ Portfolio Data Returned Portfolio Components HOLDINGS Stocks and securities you currently own in your Demat account. Remain until you sell them. Reliance × 20 | TCS × 10 | Infosys × 15 POSITIONS Currently active trades — intraday (Day) and carry-forward (Net) positions. Buy Reliance @ ₹2800 → hold / sell same day AVERAGE PRICE Average cost per share across multiple buy transactions. (10×₹100 + 10×₹120) ÷ 20 = ₹110 MARKET VALUE Current worth of your holdings at live market price. 20 shares × ₹2900 = ₹58,000 INVESTED VALUE Total amount you originally paid to buy the shares. 20 shares × ₹2800 = ₹56,000 P&L Profit or loss — difference between Market Value and Invested Value. ₹58,000 − ₹56,000 = ₹2,000 Profit Position Types Day Position Intraday trades opened and closed on the same trading day. Buy Reliance @ ₹2800 → Sell @ ₹2820 same day Profit = ₹20 per share (Realized) Net Position Positions carried forward beyond the current trading session. Buy TCS today → Hold for several days Profit is Unrealized until you sell Portfolio API Endpoints Holdings GET /interactive/portfolio/holdings All stocks currently owned. Includes symbol, qty, avg price, current price, market value. Long-term delivery stocks in Demat Positions GET /interactive/portfolio/positions Active positions — intraday and carry-forward. Includes realized & unrealized P&L. Open trades and their current status Funds GET /interactive/user/balance Available cash, used margin, and full balance breakdown across all segments. Cash available + margin limits What Happens Internally? 1 User requests portfolio — API call with valid session token 2 Portfolio API validates session — checks auth token 3 Broker server fetches data — holdings and positions from database 4 Market prices retrieved — live LTP fetched for each instrument 5 P&L calculated — realized and unrealized computed per position 6 Portfolio data returned — full structured JSON response P&L Formulas Realized P&L Profit / loss from closed trades Locked in when you complete a trade — Buy + Sell same stock. FORMULA Realized P&L = (Sell Price − Buy Price) × Qty EXAMPLE Bought @ ₹100 Sold @ ₹120 Profit +₹20 per share Unrealized P&L Floating profit / loss on open positions Fluctuates with market price. Not in funds until position is closed. FORMULA Long : P&L = (LTP − Avg Buy Price) × Open Qty Short : P&L = (Avg Sell Price − LTP) × Open Qty EXAMPLE (LONG) Bought Reliance @ ₹2,800 Current LTP ₹2,900 Unrealized +₹100 per share Why Traders Use Portfolio APIs Investment Tracking Monitor all investments across exchanges in one unified dashboard. Risk Management Understand exposure to different stocks and sectors, and limit concentration risk. Performance Analysis Measure gains and losses precisely — both realized and unrealized — over any period. Portfolio Diversification Spread investment across Banking, IT, Pharma, FMCG to reduce market volatility risk. Automated Management Build robo-advisors and rebalancing bots that act on live portfolio data. Diversification Example Concentrated Risk 100% in one sector — if that sector crashes, your entire portfolio suffers. ₹1,00,000 → All in IT stocks Diversified Spread across sectors — one sector falls but others can offset the loss. Banking 25% | IT 25% | Pharma 25% | FMCG 25% In Simple Words: A Portfolio is a complete collection of all investments owned by a user. Portfolio APIs return holdings, positions, investment value, market value, and profit or loss — allowing traders and apps to track and manage investments efficiently. Think of it as a report card for your investments , showing where your money is and how it is performing.

docs.text: Position Convert Change the product type of an open position without closing the trade — for example, convert Intraday (MIS) to Delivery (CNC) to hold overnight. No Re-entry Needed MIS → CNC / NRML Avoid Auto Square-off Qty & P&L Preserved What is Position Convert? Position Convert is the process of changing the product type of an existing open position without closing the trade. Only the product category changes — the stock, quantity, buy/sell price, and P&L all remain the same. Why is Position Conversion Needed? Bought intraday but want to hold it for several days Accidentally selected the wrong product type on order placement Want to avoid automatic intraday square-off Examples EXAMPLE 1 Intraday → Delivery You buy 100 shares of ABC Ltd. at ₹500 as Intraday (MIS) . Later you decide to keep them as an investment. Intraday MIS → Delivery CNC Shares will be credited to your Demat after settlement (subject to sufficient funds). EXAMPLE 2 Delivery → Intraday You accidentally placed a Delivery (CNC) order but only wanted to trade for the day. Delivery CNC → Intraday MIS Now the trade is treated as an intraday position (if broker allows it). Common Position Conversions From To Note Intraday (MIS) Delivery (CNC) Most common — hold overnight Delivery (CNC) Intraday (MIS) If allowed by broker Margin Delivery Convert margin position to delivery Delivery Margin Subject to broker rules NRML MIS For derivatives, if supported MIS NRML For derivatives, if supported What Changes During Conversion? ✔ STAYS THE SAME ● Stock or contract ● Quantity ● Buy / Sell price ● Average price ● P&L (based on market) ✦ WHAT CHANGES ● Product type (MIS / CNC / NRML) ● Margin requirement ● Square-off behavior ● Settlement treatment When Can You Convert? ✔ Position is still open ✔ Market is open (within conversion window) ✔ Sufficient funds or margin available ✔ Exchange and broker support the conversion Position Conversion Workflow Place an Order ↓ Position is Created ↓ Need to Change Product Type? ↓ Submit Position Conversion Request via API ↓ Broker Validates Funds, Margin & Rules ↓ Position Continues with New Product Type ✔ Real-Life Example Rahul buys 100 shares of XYZ Ltd. at ₹300 as Intraday (MIS) . By afternoon, the stock is rising and he believes it will continue for a few days. He converts the position. BEFORE MIS Intraday → AFTER CNC Delivery Shares are credited to Rahul's Demat after settlement. He can now hold them for as long as he wants. Benefits Avoid automatic intraday square-off Correct an incorrect product selection Hold shares for the long term Adjust strategy without a new order Save time & brokerage on re-entry ⚠️ Things to Remember: Not every position can be converted. Some brokers charge additional fees or require extra margin. Derivative positions (Futures & Options) may have different conversion rules. Once a position is fully closed , it cannot be converted. In Simple Words: Position Convert means changing the product type of an open position (such as Intraday to Delivery) without closing the trade. This lets you continue holding the same position under a different trading category, subject to your broker's rules. Convert Position API Convert Position API enables users to convert their open positions from NRML (Normal) to MIS (Margin Intraday Square-off) or vice versa, provided there is sufficient margin or funds in the account to complete the conversion. "success position convert" } Copy Code Examples CURL Python curl --location --request PUT 'https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/interactive/portfolio/positions/convert' \ --header 'Authorization: xxxxxx' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{' "exchangeSegment": "NSECM" , "exchangeInstrumentID": 2885 , "targetQty": 1 , "isDayWise": true , "oldProductType": "NRML" , docs.text: Positions View and manage your currently active open trades — both intraday (MIS) and overnight (NRML/CNC) positions across all exchange segments. Day-wise & Net-wise Real-time MTM PnL Product Conversion All Segments What is a Position? A Position shows how many shares or contracts you currently hold in a particular security after all your buy and sell trades. Think of it as a real-time summary of your activity for each stock or instrument. Simple Example — ACC Ltd. Action Quantity Running Position ▲ Buy 100 +100 ▲ Buy 50 +150 ▼ Sell 30 +120 Your current position is 120 shares of ACC Ltd. Types of Positions ▲ Long Position You have bought more than you sold . You own shares. Buy 100 shares Sell 20 shares Position: +80 (Long) ▼ Short Position You have sold more than you bought . Allowed in intraday & derivatives. Sell 100 shares Buy 40 shares Position: −60 (Short) ● Closed Position All bought quantity is sold (or vice versa). No open holding remains. Buy 100 shares Sell 100 shares Position: 0 (Closed) Position Information A position entry includes the following key fields: Field Description Symbol Name of the stock or contract Exchange Exchange where it is traded — NSE, BSE, MCX, etc. ProductType Delivery, Intraday, Margin, Futures, Options, etc. BuyQuantity Total quantity purchased SellQuantity Total quantity sold NetQuantity Buy Quantity − Sell Quantity BuyAveragePrice Average price of all buy trades SellAveragePrice Average price of all sell trades LTP Last Traded Price — latest market price of the security MTM / P&L Current profit or loss based on market price Position vs Holdings POSITION ▸ Shows your active trading position ▸ Includes intraday and derivative trades ▸ Changes throughout the trading day ▸ Can be Long or Short HOLDINGS ▸ Shows stocks owned in your Demat account ▸ Only delivery shares are shown ▸ Changes only when delivery is credited/debited ▸ Always represents owned shares Real-Life Example Imagine you buy 100 shares of XYZ Ltd. at ₹500 , then sell 40 shares at ₹520 . BUY QTY 100 SELL QTY 40 NET POSITION 60 MARKET PRICE ₹530 Your remaining 60 shares are valued at the latest price of ₹530 . Unrealized P&L = (530 − 500) × 60 = ₹1,800 profit . Why Positions Are Important Track your current open trades Monitor real-time P&L See quantity you own or need to close Make informed buy/sell decisions Manage risk by monitoring exposure Avoid auto square-off penalties In Simple Words: A Position is a real-time summary of your trading activity for a particular stock or contract. It shows how many units you currently hold (or owe), along with their current profit or loss. Get Positions Fetch all open positions — day-wise and net-wise — for the authenticated user. ENDPOINT GET https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000 /interactive/portfolio/positions Requires: valid Authorization token Copy URL Request Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description dayOrNet docs.text: Order Book A complete record of all buy and sell orders placed in your trading account — including their current status, execution details, and full order lifecycle. All Order Statuses Real-time Updates Modify & Cancel All Segments What is an Order Book? The Order Book is a record of all the orders you have placed with your trading account . It shows the current status of each order — whether it is pending, executed, cancelled, rejected, or partially filled. An Order Book helps you track every order from the moment it is placed until it is completed or cancelled. Simple Definition: An Order Book is a list of all your buy and sell orders, along with their current status and details. Why is the Order Book Important? Track all placed orders Check if order is executed or pending View order price & quantity details Modify or cancel eligible orders Monitor partially executed orders Avoid missed or duplicate orders How an Order Moves Through the Order Book 1 Place Order 2 Order Received by Exchange 3 Order Pending — waiting to match 4 Matched with Another Order ✓ Order Executed → Appears in Trade Book & Position If the order cannot be executed, it may instead become: Cancelled — user or broker cancelled before execution Rejected — exchange or broker rejected the order Example Order Book Order ID Symbol Side Qty Price Status 10001 ABC Ltd. BUY 100 ₹500 Filled 10002 XYZ Ltd. SELL 50 ₹700 Pending 10003 PQR Ltd. BUY 200 ₹150 Partially Filled 10004 LMN Ltd. SELL 100 ₹400 Cancelled Common Order Statuses PENDING The order has been accepted but not yet executed. Buy 100 shares @ ₹500 Current Market Price = ₹505 Status: Pending FILLED The entire order has been successfully executed. Buy 100 shares @ ₹500 Filled Quantity = 100 Status: Filled PARTIALLY FILLED Only part of the requested quantity has been executed. Buy Quantity = 100 | Executed = 60 Remaining = 40 Status: Partially Filled CANCELLED / REJECTED Cancelled by user/broker, or rejected by exchange due to invalid price, quantity, or insufficient funds. Buy 100 shares — cancelled before execution Reasons: Insufficient funds · Invalid price · Market closed Status: Cancelled / Rejected Order Book vs Trade Book vs Position ORDER BOOK ▸ Shows all placed orders ▸ Includes pending, cancelled & filled ▸ Tracks order lifecycle TRADE BOOK ▸ Shows only executed trades ▸ Only completed executions ▸ Confirms completed trades POSITION ▸ Current open quantity ▸ Only executed quantities ▸ Tracks current holdings Real-Life Example Rahul places an order to buy 100 shares of ABC Ltd. at ₹500 . 1 Order appears in Order Book — Status: Pending 2 Exchange executes 60 shares — Status: Partially Filled 3 Remaining 40 shares are executed — Status: Filled ✓ Trade appears in Trade Book and Rahul's Position shows 100 shares In Simple Words: The Order Book is a complete record of all your buy and sell orders. It shows each order's details and current status — Pending, Filled, Partially Filled, Cancelled, or Rejected — so you can monitor every order from placement to completion. Get Order Book Fetch all orders placed by the authenticated user along with their current status. Calculate P&L Use executed prices to calculate trading profit or loss. Trading History Keep a record of all completed buy and sell transactions. Reconcile Orders Match executed trades with the corresponding orders. Performance Analysis Review past trades to evaluate trading performance. !!! tip If an order was partially filled in multiple executions, you will see multiple rows in the Trade Book for the same AppOrderID — one row per execution.

docs.text: Authentication Authentication (Auth) is the process of verifying a user's identity before allowing access to Market Data APIs — the security check that confirms you are an authorized user. Secure access Prevents unauthorized use Account protection API usage control Request tracking Valid users only How Authentication Works Send Login Request → Server Validates → Token Generated → Token Returned → API Access Granted Login & Logout APIs Login (POST) You are logging in to the authentication using the POST method request. You will receive a token parameter in the response which is used to authenticate subsequent requests. All request headers should have the content type set to application/json . URL https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/auth/login Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description secretKey RawString Y The predefined secret key assigned to the client appKey RawString Y The App Key issued for the client Request Body JSON { "secretKey" : "xxxxxxxxxxxx" , "appKey" : "xxxxxxxxxxxx" } Response Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Description token Token The authentication token used to authorize every subsequent request userID UserID UserID of the logged-in client appVersion AppVersion Market Data App version application_expiry_date ApplicationExpiryDate Application key expiry date Response Body JSON { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-response-0010" , "description" : "Provided Valid Credentials" , "result" : { "token" : "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." , "userID" : "DVJ8588" , "appVersion" : "5.0.15" , "application_expiry_date" : "30-12-2028" } } Logout (DELETE) You are logging out of the application using the DELETE method request. You will need to pass the Token/Authorization value in the request header. You will receive a success/failure message in the response. URL https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/auth/logout Response Body JSON { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-login-0005" , "description" : "successfully logged out" , "result" : {} } Step 1 — Send Login Request The user provides credentials: { "secretKey" : "xxxxx" , "appKey" : "xxxxx" , "source" : "WebAPI" } Step 2 — Server Validates Credentials ✔ App Key valid? Checks if the App Key exists and is active. ✔ Secret Key valid? Matches the Secret Key against stored records. ✔ Access rights? Confirms the user has permission to access data. Step 3 — Token Generated & Returned If validation succeeds, the server returns an access token: { "token" : "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni..." } Step 4 — Use Token in Future Requests Include the token in every API request header: Authorization : Bearer <token> What is an Access Token? WITHOUT TOKEN Login every single API call → WITH TOKEN Login once → use token for all calls Authentication Failure Errors Invalid Credentials "type" : "error" , "description" : "Invalid App Key" Expired Token "type" : "error" , "description" : "Session Expired" Unauthorized Access "type" : "error" , "description" : "Authentication Failed" APIs That Require Authentication Authentication is the first API call before accessing any of these: Real-time Quotes OHLC Data Market Depth Instruments WebSocket Historical Data Security Best Practices Keep Keys Private Never expose App Key, Secret Key, or Access Token in public code or repositories. Use HTTPS Always communicate through secure encrypted connections. Store Tokens Securely Avoid storing tokens in client-side code or public repositories. Refresh Expired Sessions Generate a new token when the current session expires. Real-Life Analogy Office Building Building = Market Data API ID Card Check = Authentication Access Card = Token Office Entry = API Access ✔ Key Takeaway Without the ID card, you cannot enter the building. Similarly, without authentication, you cannot access market data .

docs.text: Data Types & Business Rules The following data types, data values, business types, and validation rules define the structure and constraints for all Market Data API fields. DataName DataType Size Description ExchangeInstrumentID Integer 10 Unique instrument identifier assigned by the exchange. ExchangeSegment Integer 10 Exchange segment this instrument belongs to. InstrumentType Integer 10 Type of the instrument (Equity, Futures, Options, etc.). Name String 50 Name of the instrument. Description String MAX Full description of the instrument. ISIN String 20 International Securities Identification Number. ExchangeSeries String 10 Exchange series identifier for the instrument. DisplayInMarketWatchFlag Integer 5 Flag to indicate if the instrument should be displayed in market watch. ExchangeInstrumentStatus Integer 10 Current status of the instrument on the exchange. ContractExpiration Long 20 Expiration date/time of the contract. ContractType Integer 10 Type classification of the contract. ContractSubType Integer 10 Sub-type classification of the contract. StrikePrice Double (15,4) Strike price for options contracts. UnderlyingInstrumentID Integer 10 Exchange instrument ID of the underlying asset. UnderlyingIndexOption Integer 10 Underlying index for index options. OpenPrice Double (15,4) Opening price for the current session. High Double (15,4) Highest traded price during the session. Low Double (15,4) Lowest traded price during the session. Close Double (15,4) Closing price for the session. PreviousClose Double (15,4) Closing price from the previous session. LastTradedPrice Double (15,4) Most recent traded price of the instrument. LastTradedQuantity Long 15 Quantity traded in the most recent trade. AverageTradedPrice Double (15,4) Volume-weighted average traded price for the session. Volume Long 15 Total traded volume in the session. TotalValueTraded Double (15,4) Total monetary value of all trades in the session. TotalSellQuantity Long 15 Total quantity available on the sell side of the order book. TotalBuyQuantity Long 15 Total quantity available on the buy side of the order book. OrderBookDepth Integer 10 Number of price levels available in the order book. TokenID Integer 10 Unique token identifier for the instrument. Expiry String 20 Expiry date of the contract in string format. ContractLotSize Integer 10 Standard lot size for the contract. ContractScaledLotSize Integer 10 Scaled lot size for the contract. LotSizeInformation Integer 10 Additional lot size details for the instrument. OptionType Integer 10 Option type identifier (CE, PE, etc.). Multiplier Double (15,4) Price multiplier applied to the instrument value. Bid Double (15,4) Best bid price in the order book. Ask Double (15,4) Best ask price in the order book. BidSize Long 15 Quantity available at the best bid price. AskSize Long 15 Quantity available at the best ask price. IssuedCapital Double (15,4) Total capital issued by the company. FreefloatHolding Double (15,4) Percentage of shares available for public trading. ContractLotSizeMultiplier Integer 10 Multiplier for the contract lot size. ContractLotSizeMultiplierScaling Integer 10 Scaling factor for the lot size multiplier. TickSize Double (15,4) Minimum price movement allowed for the instrument. LastUpdateTime String 50 Timestamp of the last data update. PriceBand Integer 10 Upper/lower price band limits for the instrument. Delivery Integer 10 Delivery mode applicable for the instrument. ContractMaxQuantity Integer 10 Maximum quantity allowed per contract order. ContractMaxQuantityScaling Integer 10 Scaling factor for the maximum contract quantity. BoardLotQuantity Integer 10 Minimum number of units that can be traded in one lot. FaceValue Integer 10 Face value of the security per unit/share. Spread Integer 10 Difference between best buy and sell price. CallAuction1Flag Boolean 5 Indicates if a first call auction is applicable. docs.text: Enums with Numeric Constants Enums are predefined sets of values used by the Market Data API to represent options, states, or configurations — using compact numeric codes for speed and consistency. 1. ExchangeSegments Enum Name Numeric Code Description NSECM 1 - NSE Cash Market segment for trading equity shares. - Used to buy and sell stocks listed on NSE. - Example: Reliance, TCS, Infosys shares. NSEFO 2 - NSE Futures & Options segment. - Used for trading futures and options contracts. - Example: NIFTY Futures, BANKNIFTY Options. NSECD 3 - NSE Currency Derivatives segment. - Used for trading currency futures and options. - Example: USD/INR, EUR/INR contracts. NSECO 4 - NSE Commodity segment. - Used for commodity derivative trading on NSE. - Example: Gold, Silver, Crude Oil contracts. BSECM 11 - BSE Cash Market segment for equity trading. - Used to buy and sell stocks listed on BSE. - Example: Stocks traded on the Bombay Stock Exchange. BSEFO 12 - BSE Futures & Options segment. - Used for trading derivative contracts on BSE. - Example: SENSEX Futures and Options. BSECD 13 - BSE Currency Derivatives segment. - Used for trading currency-based derivative contracts. - Example: USD/INR currency futures. MCXFO 51 - MCX Futures & Options segment. - Used for commodity derivatives trading. - Example: Gold, Silver, Crude Oil Futures. NCDEX 21 - National Commodity & Derivatives Exchange segment. - Used mainly for agricultural commodity trading. - Example: Cotton, Soybean, Chana Futures. 2. MarketType Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1 - Represents the regular trading session of the exchange. - Market data is received for normal buy and sell activities. - Most stock and derivative trading happens in this market type. Oddlot 2 - Used for trades involving quantities smaller than the standard market lot. - Commonly used when the quantity does not meet the regular lot size. - Market data is published separately from normal trades. Retaildebt 3 - Represents the retail debt market segment. - Used for trading bonds and other debt securities by retail investors. - Market data includes prices and trades of debt instruments. Auction 4 - Represents the auction market session. - Used for special auction-based trading conducted by the exchange. - Orders are matched through an auction process instead of continuous trading. CallAuction1 5 - Represents the first type of call auction market session. - Orders are collected first and then executed together at a single price. - Commonly used during special auction periods. CallAuction2 6 - Represents the second type of call auction market session. - Similar to CallAuction1, orders are matched in a batch at one price. - Used for specific exchange-defined auction sessions. 3. InstrumentType Enum Name Numeric Code Description Futures 1 - A Futures contract is an agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date. - Traders use it to earn profit from price movements without owning the asset immediately. - It is commonly used for stocks, commodities, currencies, and market indices. Options 2 - An Option gives the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price. - It helps traders manage risk or profit from expected price changes. - The buyer pays a small fee called a premium to get this right. Spread 4 - A Spread means taking two related trading positions at the same time. - One position is bought and the other is sold to reduce risk. - Profit comes from the difference in price movement between the two positions. Equity 8 - Equity represents ownership in a company through shares or stocks. - When you buy equity shares, you become a part-owner of that company. - Your profit can come from share price growth and dividends. Spot 16 - Spot trading means buying or selling an asset immediately at the current market price. - The ownership and payment are usually settled right away. - It is the simplest form of trading used in stocks, currencies, and commodities. PreferenceShares 32 - Preference Shares are special shares that give fixed dividends before equity shareholders are paid. - They usually have lower risk compared to ordinary shares. - However, preference shareholders often have limited or no voting rights. Debentures 64 - Debentures are a type of loan given by investors to a company. - The company promises to pay regular interest and return the money after a fixed period. - Debenture holders are creditors, not owners of the company. Warrants 128 - A Warrant gives the holder the right to buy company shares at a fixed price in the future. - It is usually valid for a longer period than options. - Investors use warrants when they expect the company's share price to rise. Miscellaneous 256 - Miscellaneous includes financial instruments that do not fit into common categories. - These may have unique features, purposes, or trading rules. - Examples can vary depending on the market or financial institution. MutualFund 512 - A Mutual Fund collects money from many investors and invests it in different assets. - Professional fund managers make investment decisions on behalf of investors. - It helps people diversify investments and reduce individual investment risk. 4. XTS Message Code Enum Name Numeric Code Description TouchLineEvent 1501 - A TouchLineEvent occurs whenever the latest market price (Last Traded Price) changes. - It provides quick updates about the current trading activity of a stock or instrument. - Traders use it to monitor real-time price movements and market direction. MarketDepthEvent 1502 - A MarketDepthEvent shows the list of buy and sell orders currently available in the market. - It helps traders see demand, supply, and liquidity at different price levels. - This information is useful for understanding market strength and planning trades. CandleDataEvent 1505 - A CandleDataEvent provides price data in candlestick format for a specific time period. - Each candle contains Open, High, Low, and Close (OHLC) prices. - Traders use candlestick data to analyze trends, patterns, and market behavior. OpenInterestEvent 1510 - An OpenInterestEvent shows the total number of active futures or options contracts in the market. - It indicates how much money and participation are present in a particular contract. - Rising open interest often suggests stronger market activity and trader interest. 5. Exchange Trading Session Enum Name Numeric Code Description PreOpenStart 0 - This is the beginning of the pre-open market session before regular trading starts. - During this time, traders can place, modify, or cancel orders. - The exchange collects orders to determine the opening price. PreOpenEnd 1 - This marks the end of the pre-open session. - The exchange processes all collected orders and calculates the opening market price. - Regular trading is about to begin after this phase. NormalStart 2 - This is the start of the normal trading session. - Buy and sell orders are matched continuously in real time. - Most market trading activity happens during this period. NormalEnd 4 - This indicates the end of the regular trading session. - New trades under normal market rules stop after this point. - The market then moves to the next session, such as post-closing. PostClosingStart 8 - This is the beginning of the post-closing session after normal trading ends. - Certain order types may still be accepted depending on exchange rules. - It helps complete settlement-related or closing-price activities. PostClosingEnd 16 - This marks the end of the post-closing session. - All special post-market activities are completed. - The market prepares to move into the closed state. Closed 32 - The market is completely closed for trading. - No new buy or sell transactions can be executed. - This usually occurs after market hours, weekends, or holidays. None 256 - This means no market session status is currently assigned or available. - It may be used as a default or placeholder value in the system. - Applications often show this when session information is unavailable. 6. Exchange Market Type Enum Name Numeric Code Description Normal 1 - Regular trading process jahan exchange ke standard rules follow hote hain. - Sabhi orders normal market timings mein execute kiye jaate hain. - Daily buying aur selling ke liye sabse commonly used category hai. OddLot 2 - Jab quantity standard trading lot se kam ya alag hoti hai tab use kiya jaata hai. - Aise orders special handling ke saath process hote hain. - Small quantity transactions ke liye suitable hai. RetailDebt 3 - Retail investors ke liye debt instruments (Bonds, NCDs, etc.) ki trading. - Ismein fixed-income securities ko buy ya sell kiya ja sakta hai. - Regular equity trading se alag debt market transactions ke liye use hota hai. Auction 4 - Auction session mein pending ya unsettled positions ko resolve karne ke liye use hota hai. - Exchange required securities ki buying ya selling auction process se karwata hai. - Settlement obligations complete karne mein madad karta hai. CallAuction1 5 - Pre-defined auction window jahan orders collect kiye jaate hain. - Matching ek fixed time par hoti hai, continuously nahi. - Price discovery aur fair order execution ke liye use kiya jaata hai. CallAuction2 6 - Call Auction ka doosra phase ya session. - Collected orders ko match karke final execution kiya jaata hai. - Market mein transparency aur efficient price determination ensure karta hai. 7. CallAuction Type Enum Name Numeric Code Description NonCallAuction 0 - Regular market segment jahan trading continuous basis par hoti hai. - Orders aate hi matching rules ke according execute hote hain. - Call Auction mechanism is segment mein apply nahi hota. PreOpen 1 - Market open hone se pehle orders collect aur match kiye jaate hain. - Is session ka purpose opening price determine karna hota hai. - Trading start hone se pehle fair price discovery ensure karta hai. IPOPreOpen 2 - Naye IPO listed stock ke liye special pre-open session. - Orders collect karke initial listing price discover ki jaati hai. - Listing day par smooth aur transparent market opening mein madad karta hai. RelistPreOpen 3 - Relisted security ke liye market open hone se pehle ka session. - Orders collect karke opening price determine ki jaati hai. - Relisting ke baad fair trading start karne mein help karta hai. Illiquid 4 - Kam trading volume aur low market activity wali securities. - Inmein buyers aur sellers ki availability limited ho sakti hai. - Price movements comparatively zyada volatile ho sakte hain. SME 5 - Small and Medium Enterprises ki listed securities ka segment. - Yeh platform growing businesses ko capital raise karne ka mauka deta hai. - SME companies ke shares ki trading ke liye use kiya jaata hai. SCAS 6 - Special Call Auction Session ke under aane wali securities. - Orders ek fixed auction process ke through collect aur match kiye jaate hain. - Price discovery aur controlled trading environment provide karta hai. 8. BookType Enum Name Numeric Code Description None 0 - No special order condition is applied to the trade. - The order follows the default market trading process. - Used for standard buy and sell transactions. Regular 1 - Order is placed in the normal trading market segment. - It follows standard exchange rules and timings. - Most day-to-day trading activities use this category. SpecialTerms 2 - Order is subject to specific exchange-defined conditions. - Execution may follow additional settlement or trading rules. - Used when standard trading terms do not apply. StopLoss 3 - Order is triggered only when a specified price is reached. - Helps limit potential losses in volatile markets. - Commonly used for risk management and capital protection. Negotiated 4 - Trade is executed based on terms agreed between parties. - Price and quantity are decided before execution. - Typically used for special or large-value transactions. OddLot 5 - Order quantity is smaller than the standard market lot size. - It allows trading of non-standard share quantities. - Commonly used for small holdings or partial transactions. Spot 6 - Trade settlement is completed on the same day or immediately. - Ownership transfer happens faster than regular settlement. - Used when quick settlement is required. Auction 7 - Order participates in an exchange auction session. - Matching occurs through an auction-based price discovery process. - Used for special market events and settlement requirements. CallAuction1 11 - Orders are collected during the first call auction session. - Execution happens at a single price after order collection. - Helps determine a fair market price before trading. CallAuction2 12 - Orders are collected during the second call auction session. - Matching is performed at a calculated auction price. - Provides additional price discovery and orderly execution. 9. OptionType Enum Name Numeric Code Description CA 1 - CA — Corporate Action - Provides information about company actions such as dividends, stock splits, bonus issues, and mergers. - Helps track changes that can affect a stock's value and shareholder holdings. PA 2 - PA — Price Action - Provides data about how a stock's price moves over time. - Includes trends, price changes, highs, lows, and market movement patterns. CE 3 - CE — Corporate Event - Provides details about important company-related events. - Includes earnings announcements, board meetings, annual meetings, and disclosures. PE 4 - PE — Price Event - Provides alerts or records of significant price-related movements. - Includes sharp price increases, decreases, or predefined price threshold triggers. None 5 - No specific event type is selected. - Data will not be filtered by any event category. - Use this option when you want the default or unfiltered market data. 10. PublishFormat Enum Name Numeric Code Description Binary 1 - Returns market data in a compact binary format for faster processing and lower bandwidth usage. - Optimized for high-performance applications that require maximum speed and efficiency. - Best suited for systems that can parse and decode binary data formats. JSON 2 - Returns market data in a human-readable JSON format. - Easy to integrate, debug, and use across most programming languages and applications. - Best suited for development, testing, and standard API integrations. 11. BroadCastMode Enum Name Numeric Code Description Full 1 - Returns the complete set of available market data for the requested instrument or event. - Includes all relevant fields and details without any data reduction. - Best suited when comprehensive information is required for analysis or reporting. Partial 2 - Returns only a subset of the available market data. - Includes essential fields to reduce response size and improve performance. - Best suited when only key information is needed for faster processing. 12. Socket Event Enum Name Description joined - WebSocket Joined - Sent when a client successfully connects and joins the WebSocket channel. - Confirms that the real-time data stream is active and ready. error - Error Event - Indicates a failure during WebSocket connection or request processing. - Includes invalid request, authentication failure, or system error. warning - Warning Message - Non-critical advisory message from the server. - Example: rate limit approaching or deprecated API usage detected. success - Success Response - Confirms that a client request was processed successfully. - Example: subscription to an instrument acknowledged.

docs.text: Socket Streaming Socket Streaming creates a live connection between your application and the Market Data server. Once connected, market updates are automatically pushed in real time — no repeated requests needed. Real-time updates Low latency No repeated calls WebSocket based Live price & depth Efficient bandwidth How Socket Streaming Works Connect → Subscribe → Receive Updates → Unsubscribe → Disconnect 1. Connect Establish a WebSocket connection with the Market Data server using your authentication token. 2. Subscribe Subscribe to instruments using Exchange Segment and Exchange Instrument ID. Server starts tracking them. 3. Receive Updates Server automatically pushes data whenever market changes occur. No additional requests needed. 4. Unsubscribe Stop receiving updates for specific instruments at any time without closing the connection. 5. Disconnect Close the WebSocket connection when streaming is no longer required. docs.text: Socket Subscription Socket Subscription tells the Market Data server which instruments you want to track. After subscribing, live market updates for those instruments are automatically pushed to your application in real time. Live updates Instrument tracking No repeated requests Price streaming Low latency Multi-instrument How Subscription Works Connect & Auth → Send Subscription → Server Registers → Live Data Pushed → Unsubscribe Information Required exchangeSegment : "NSECM" // e.g. NSECM, NSEFO, BSECM exchangeInstrumentID : 2885 // unique instrument identifier messageCode : 1501 // 1501=Touchline, 1502=Depth Data Available Through Subscription Touchline Data Last Traded Price (LTP) Open / High / Low / Close Volume Market Depth Data Best Buy Prices Best Sell Prices Bid & Ask Quantities Index Data Live Index Values Change Percentage Change Trade Data Trade Price Trade Quantity Trade Time Example Workflow // Step 1 — Connect to WebSocket server connect ( "wss://marketdata.server" , token) // Step 2 — Subscribe to RELIANCE and TCS subscribe ({ instruments : [ { exchangeSegment : "NSECM" , exchangeInstrumentID : 2885 }, // RELIANCE { exchangeSegment : "NSECM" , exchangeInstrumentID : 11536 } // TCS ], messageCode : 1501 }) // Step 3 — Receive live updates automatically onData (event → process price update) // Step 4 — Add more instruments anytime subscribe ([{ exchangeSegment : "NSEFO" , exchangeInstrumentID : 35001 }]) // Step 5 — Unsubscribe when no longer needed unsubscribe ([ "NSECM:2885" ]) Benefits Real-time Updates Data pushed instantly on market change Low Latency Minimal delay between event and delivery Reduced API Calls No repeated polling for updates Efficient Bandwidth Only changed data transmitted Better Trading UX Smooth, responsive app experience Subscribe to Socket This API request is used to subscribe to market data over a WebSocket connection for specified exchange instruments and message codes provided in the request. Upon successful subscription, the user receives an acknowledgment response containing the latest quote data along with the remaining subscription count, which is AppKey-specific and configurable via the API dashboard. Once subscribed, real-time market data for the specified instrument(s) will be continuously streamed on the market data WebSocket. URL PUT https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/instruments/subscription 📋 Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description instruments Array Y Array of instrument objects exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment Y ExchangeSegment exchangeInstrumentID ExchangeInstrumentID Y Exchange Scrip code or Symbol Token is unique identifier MessageCode Integer Y It is system generated message code Request Body JSON { "instruments" : [ { "exchangeSegment" : 1 , "exchangeInstrumentID" : 22 } ], "xtsMessageCode" : 1582 } 📋 Copy Response Body JSON { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-session-0001" , "description" : "Instrument subscribed successfully!" , "result" : { "mdp" : 1501 , "quotesList" : [ { "exchangeSegment" : 1 , "exchangeInstrumentID" : 22 } ], "listQuotes" : [ "{\"MessageCode\":1501,\"ExchangeSegment\":1,\"ExchangeInstrumentID\":\"22\",\"LastTradedPrice\":1723,\"LastTradedQunatity\":15,\"TotalBuyQuantity\":18446,\"TotalSellQuantity\":25283,\"TotalTradedQuantity\":189238,\"Average...\"}" ], "Remaining_Subscription_Count" : 48 } } 📋 Copy Unsubscribe to Socket This API request is used to unsubscribe from market data streaming for instruments that are already subscribed. Upon successful unsubscription, the server sends an acknowledgment confirming the unsubscription, stops sending market data for the specified instrument(s) on the WebSocket, and releases the corresponding subscription count, making it available for future subscriptions. docs.text: This API request is used to subscribe to market data over a WebSocket connection for specified exchange instruments and message codes provided in the request. Upon successful subscription, the user receives an acknowledgment response containing the latest quote data along with the remaining subscription count, which is AppKey-specific and configurable via the API dashboard. Once subscribed, real-time market data for the specified instrument(s) will be continuously streamed on the market data WebSocket. URL PUT https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/instruments/subscription 📋 Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description instruments Array Y Array of instrument objects exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment Y ExchangeSegment exchangeInstrumentID ExchangeInstrumentID Y Exchange Scrip code or Symbol Token is unique identifier MessageCode Integer Y It is system generated message code Request Body JSON { "instruments" : [ { "exchangeSegment" : 1 , "exchangeInstrumentID" : 22 } ], "xtsMessageCode" : 1582 } 📋 Copy Response Body JSON { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-session-0001" , "description" : "Instrument subscribed successfully!" , "result" : { "mdp" : 1501 , "quotesList" : [ { "exchangeSegment" : 1 , "exchangeInstrumentID" : 22 } ], "listQuotes" : [ "{\"MessageCode\":1501,\"ExchangeSegment\":1,\"ExchangeInstrumentID\":\"22\",\"LastTradedPrice\":1723,\"LastTradedQunatity\":15,\"TotalBuyQuantity\":18446,\"TotalSellQuantity\":25283,\"TotalTradedQuantity\":189238,\"Average...\"}" ], "Remaining_Subscription_Count" : 48 } } 📋 Copy

docs.text: This API request is used to unsubscribe from market data streaming for instruments that are already subscribed. Upon successful unsubscription, the server sends an acknowledgment confirming the unsubscription, stops sending market data for the specified instrument(s) on the WebSocket, and releases the corresponding subscription count, making it available for future subscriptions. URL PUT https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/instruments/subscription 📋 Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description instruments Array Y Array of instrument objects exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment Y ExchangeSegment exchangeInstrumentID ExchangeInstrumentID Y Exchange Scrip code or Symbol Token is unique identifier xtsMessageCode xtsMessageCode Y It is system generated message code Request Body JSON { "instruments" : [ { "exchangeSegment" : 1 , "exchangeInstrumentID" : 22 } ], "xtsMessageCode" : 1502 } 📋 Copy Response Body JSON [ { "type" : "success" , "code" : "s-response-0001" , "description" : "Instrument subscription deleted!" , "result" : { "Remaining_Subscription_Count" : 4 } } ] 📋 Copy

docs.text: Market Depth Market Depth provides real-time visibility into the full order book — all pending buy and sell orders at every price level. It shows market liquidity, supply and demand, and potential price pressure far beyond the last traded price. Trading Terminals Liquidity Analysis Support & Resistance Algorithmic Trading Order Flow Analysis What is Market Depth? The order book is a real-time list of every pending buy and sell order for an instrument. Market Depth shows you the top 5 levels on each side — price, quantity waiting at that price, and how many individual orders are queued there. Bids (Buy Orders) Pending orders from buyers. Listed from highest to lowest price. The top bid is the highest a buyer will pay right now. Buy Side Spread The gap between the best ask and the best bid. A smaller spread means more buyers and sellers are actively trading. Center Gap Asks (Sell Orders) Pending orders from sellers. Listed from lowest to highest price. The top ask is the minimum price a seller will accept. Sell Side Live Order Book (RELIANCE) Qty Orders Price Price Orders Qty 500 4 2966.00 700 5 2965.90 1,200 9 2965.80 1,500 11 2965.70 900 6 2965.60 LTP ₹2965.50 Spread ₹0.20 2965.40 8 1,200 2965.30 13 1,800 2965.20 10 850 2965.10 6 600 2965.00 4 400 Bids (Buy Orders) Asks (Sell Orders) API Endpoint POST /apimarketdata/instruments/quotes xtsMessageCode: 1502 Market Depth data uses the same quotes endpoint as touchline data — pass xtsMessageCode: 1502 to receive the 5-level order book instead of just LTP and OHLC. Request and Response Request POST /apimarketdata/instruments/quotes Authorization: <market-token> { "instruments": [ { "exchangeInstrumentID": 2885, "exchangeSegment": 1 } ], "xtsMessageCode": 1502, "publishFormat": "JSON" } Response { "type": "success", "result": { "listQuotes": [ { "ExchangeInstrumentID": 2885, "Bids": [ { "Price": 2965.40, "Size": 1200, "TotalOrders": 8 }, { "Price": 2965.30, "Size": 1800, "TotalOrders": 13 } ], "Asks": [ { "Price": 2965.60, "Size": 900, "TotalOrders": 6 }, { "Price": 2965.70, "Size": 1500, "TotalOrders": 11 } ], "Touchline": { "LastTradedPrice": 2965.50, "BidPrice": 2965.40, "AskPrice": 2965.60 } } ] } } Response Fields Bids[ ] — Buy Side Field Description Price Bid price at this level Size Total quantity waiting at this price TotalOrders Number of individual orders at this price Asks[ ] — Sell Side Field Description Price Ask price at this level Size Total quantity available at this price TotalOrders Number of individual sellers at this price Bid, Ask, and Spread Bid Price ₹2965.40 The highest price buyers currently want to pay. If you sell at market, you get this price. Best Buy Order Spread Ask − Bid = ₹0.20 Tighter spread = more liquid. Wider spread = fewer active traders, higher cost to trade. Liquidity Signal Ask Price ₹2965.60 The lowest price sellers are willing to accept. If you buy at market, you pay this price. Best Sell Order Reading Market Liquidity The depth and size of the order book tells you how easily you can execute a large order without moving the market price. High Liquidity Large quantities on both bid and ask sides. Tight spread. Orders fill quickly at the expected price. Ideal for large orders. Tight spread (₹0.05 – ₹0.20) High total bid/ask quantity Many orders per level Low Liquidity Thin order book with small quantities. Wide spread. Large orders can move the price significantly. Risky for big trades. Wide spread (₹1 – ₹5+) Low total bid/ask quantity Few orders per level Identifying Support and Resistance Large concentrations of orders at specific price levels can act as support (large buy orders) or resistance (large sell orders). Support Level A price where a significant number of buy orders are stacked. The market often bounces back up when it reaches this level because buyers absorb selling pressure. 2965.30 — 1,800 qty 2965.20 — 850 qty 2965.00 — 12,000 qty ← Support Resistance Level A price where a significant number of sell orders are stacked. The market often struggles to break above this level because sellers keep absorbing buying pressure. 2970.00 — 15,000 qty ← Resistance 2969.50 — 600 qty 2969.00 — 900 qty Data Flow 1 Client Application Sends instrument token with xtsMessageCode 1502 2 Market Depth API Routes to the exchange order book data feed 3 Exchange Order Book Real-time snapshot of top 5 bid and ask levels 4 Depth Response Bids[ ] and Asks[ ] arrays — price, size, order count 5 Trading Terminal Renders order book, spread, and liquidity visualization Best Practices Combine with Quote Data Use market depth alongside the last traded price and OHLC to get the complete market picture before placing an order. Check Liquidity Before Large Orders Before placing a large order, verify there is enough quantity at the top levels. Thin books can cause significant slippage. Use WebSocket for Live Updates Subscribe to event code 1502 via WebSocket instead of polling. Order books update many times per second. Watch for Order Book Imbalance A large imbalance in total bid vs ask quantity often signals short-term price direction — more bids = buy pressure, more asks = sell pressure. Common Errors 404 Instrument Not Found The instrument token does not exist in the specified exchange segment. 401 Unauthorized Market data token is missing, expired, or invalid. 429 Rate Limit Exceeded Too many depth requests. Use WebSocket streaming for continuous updates. Summary Term Meaning Used For Bids Pending buy orders in the order book Identifying buy pressure and support Asks Pending sell orders in the order book Identifying sell pressure and resistance Bid Price Best (highest) price buyers will pay Market sell execution price Ask Price Best (lowest) price sellers will accept Market buy execution price Spread Ask minus Bid price Liquidity measurement Size Total quantity at a price level Order flow and liquidity analysis TotalOrders Count of individual orders at a level Market participation analysis Related APIs Instruments API Quotes API OHLC Data API WebSocket API Orders API

docs.text: OHLC Data The OHLC API provides historical candlestick price data for any tradable instrument — the foundation of every charting system, technical indicator, and backtesting engine. Each candle encodes four prices (Open, High, Low, Close) over a specific time interval. Candlestick Charts Technical Indicators Backtesting Market Trend Analysis Price Performance What is OHLC? OHLC stands for Open, High, Low, Close . Each value describes a different price point within a fixed time window — whether that window is 1 minute or 1 day. O Open The first traded price when the candle interval began. For a daily candle this is the market open price. ₹2940.00 H High The maximum price reached during the entire candle interval. Represents the top of the upper wick. ₹2975.25 L Low The minimum price reached during the entire candle interval. Represents the bottom of the lower wick. ₹2935.80 C Close The last traded price when the candle interval ended. This is the most important price for most indicators. ₹2965.50 Candlestick Structure High ₹2975.25 Close ₹2965.50 Bullish Close > Open Open ₹2940.00 Low ₹2935.80 Wick (Shadow) Thin vertical lines showing the full High-to-Low range for the interval Green Body (Bullish) Close is higher than Open — price moved up during this interval Red Body (Bearish) Close is lower than Open — price moved down during this interval API Endpoint POST /apimarketdata/instruments/ohlc Returns historical OHLC candle data for a specific instrument. Pass the exchange segment, instrument ID, time range, and compression interval in the request body. Request and Response Request Body POST /apimarketdata/instruments/ohlc Authorization: <market-token> { "exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": 2885, "startTime": "Jun 14 2026 090000", "endTime": "Jun 15 2026 153000", "compressionValue": 1 } Response { "type": "success", "result": { "dataReponse": "1718342400|2940.00|2975.25|2935.80|2965.50|1254789|0|| 1718428800|2910.00|2945.00|2895.00|2930.00|987654|0||" } } The response is pipe-separated : timestamp | open | high | low | close | volume | OI | | — each candle on its own line. Request Parameters Parameter Type Required Description exchangeSegment Integer Yes Exchange segment code (1=NSECM, 2=NSEFO, etc.) exchangeInstrumentID Integer Yes Unique instrument token from the master file startTime String Yes Start of the historical range — format: Mmm DD YYYY HHMMSS endTime String Yes End of the historical range — same format as startTime compressionValue Integer Yes Candle interval in minutes (see table below) Supported Intervals (compressionValue) 1 1 Minute Intraday scalping, HFT signals 5 5 Minutes Intraday momentum strategies 15 15 Minutes Short-term trend following 30 30 Minutes Intraday support and resistance 60 1 Hour Swing trading, multi-day trends 1440 1 Day Long-term analysis, EOD charts Response Format — Parsed Split the pipe-separated string on || to get candles, then split each candle on | to get the 7 fields: 0 Timestamp 1718342400 Unix epoch seconds — convert to datetime 1 Open 2940.00 First traded price in interval 2 High 2975.25 Highest price in interval 3 Low 2935.80 Lowest price in interval 4 Close 2965.50 Last traded price in interval 5 Volume 1254789 Total quantity traded 6 Open Interest 0 Outstanding contracts (F&O only) Intraday Candle OHLC The XTS Front-end API provides intraday archived OHLC (candlestick) data from the date of access for Equity segments of NSECM and BSECM. For FO segments, OHLC data is available only for currently traded contracts, and expired contracts are not supported. The response is delivered in candle format, including timestamp (epoch time since 1970), Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, and Open Interest (OI) . The minimum supported interval is 60 seconds (1 minute) , with additional supported intervals for the GET OHLC request detailed in the table below. Compression Value Table Expected Timeframe Compression 1 minute 60 2 minutes 120 3 minutes 180 4 minutes 240 5 minutes 300 7 minutes 420 10 minutes 600 15 minutes 900 30 minutes 1800 1 hour 3600 2 hours 7200 3 hours 10800 4 hours 14400 1 day D 1 week W 1 month M GET https://xts.rmoneyindia.co.in:3000/apibinarymarketdata/instruments/ohlc?exchangeSegment=1&exchangeInstrumentID=2885&startTime=Jan 27 2025 090000&endTime=Jan 28 2025 153000&compressionValue=D Copy Request Body Parameters Parameter Name Type Mandatory Description exchangeSegment ExchangeSegment Y Exchange segment. exchangeInstrumentID ExchangeInstrumentID Y Exchange Scrip code or Symbol Token is unique identifier. startTime StartTime Y Date and time in MMM DD YYYY HHMMSS format. Default value is Jan 27 2025 090000 endTime EndTime Y Date and time in MMM DD YYYY HHMMSS format. Default value is Jan 28 2025 153000 compressionValue CompressionValue Y String value representing time interval. Default value is D. Allowed values are In1Minute (60), In2Minute (120), In3Minute (180), In5Minute (300), In10Minute (600), In15Minute (900), In30Minute (1800), In60Minute (3600) Response Body JSON [ { "type": "success", "code": "s-instrument-0002", "description": "Data found", "result": { "exchangeSegment": 1, "exchangeInstrumentID": "22", "dataResponse": "1737331200|1316|1316|1300.25|1305.45|14040244|0|" } } ] Technical Analysis with OHLC Every major technical indicator is derived from OHLC values. Here are the most commonly computed using this data: Trend Indicators Moving Average (MA) Exponential MA (EMA) MACD SuperTrend Parabolic SAR Momentum Indicators RSI Stochastic Oscillator CCI Williams %R MFI Volatility Indicators Bollinger Bands ATR Keltner Channel Donchian Channel Volume & Price VWAP OBV Support Levels Resistance Levels Pivot Points Data Flow 1 Client Application Sends instrument token, time range, and compression interval 2 OHLC API Validates request parameters and routes to historical data store 3 Historical Market Data Fetches tick data, aggregates into OHLC candles by interval 4 OHLC Response Pipe-delimited candle data returned in chronological order 5 Charts and Analytics Parse, render, and compute indicators on the candle array Best Practices Match Interval to Strategy Use 1-min candles for intraday scalping, 1-day candles for swing trading. Fetching daily candles for a 1-min strategy wastes data resolution. Request Only What You Need Narrow the date range to the minimum required. Fetching years of 1-min data is slow and expensive — paginate if you need large historical ranges. Cache Historical Data Past candles never change. Once fetched, store them locally and only request the most recent candles on subsequent calls. Use WebSocket for Live Candles For the current (in-progress) candle, use WebSocket message code 1505 instead of polling the OHLC endpoint every second. Common Errors 400 Invalid Interval The compressionValue is not a supported minute value. 400 Invalid Date Range startTime is after endTime, or the format is incorrect. 404 Instrument Not Found The exchangeInstrumentID does not exist in the given segment. 401 Unauthorized Market data token is missing, expired, or invalid. Summary Term Meaning Used For Open First price in the interval Candle body start High Maximum price in the interval Upper wick, range analysis Low Minimum price in the interval Lower wick, support levels Close Last price in the interval Most indicators, body end compressionValue Candle duration in minutes Chart timeframe selection Bullish candle Close > Open (green) Price moved up in interval Bearish candle Close < Open (red) Price moved down in interval Related APIs Instruments API Quotes API Market Depth API WebSocket API

docs.text: Market Data API Overview The Market Data API provides real-time and historical market information for a wide range of financial instruments. API Environment URLs BASE URL https://developers.symphonyfintech.in/apibinarymarketdata Copy URL What is Market Data? Market data is information generated by exchanges during trading hours. It helps you track live prices, analyze trends, and make informed trading decisions. RELIANCE • NSE ₹2,850.00 +25.50 (0.90%) ↗ Open 2,820.00 High 2,870.00 Low 2,810.00 Prev. Close 2,824.50 Volume 1,200,000 Types of Market Data Live Data Real-time data received instantly from exchanges. Example: LTP, Bid, Ask, Volume Delayed Data Data received with a short delay (e.g., 15 minutes). Example: 15-min Delayed Data Historical Data Previously recorded data for past dates. Example: Daily, Weekly, Monthly Key Features Real-time Quotes Get the latest price, change, volume and other market details in real-time. Historical Data Access historical data for analysis, backtesting and trend identification. OHLC Data Retrieve Open, High, Low, Close data for any time interval. Market Depth View real-time buy and sell orders in the market depth (order book). Instrument Info Get details about instruments like lot size, tick size, expiry, and trading symbol. Live & Historical Support for both live market data and historical data retrieval. Market Data Workflow User Request → Market Data API → Exchange Data → API Response → Application Display Common Use Cases Trading Applications Display live market prices and execute trades. Portfolio Tracking Monitor investments and track portfolio performance. Watchlists Track your favorite stocks and market movements. Analytics Platforms Perform technical and fundamental analysis. Algorithmic Trading Use market data to build and run automated strategies. Important Note Market data changes continuously during market hours. For real-time updates, consider using WebSocket APIs. Explore Market Data APIs → TABLE OF CONTENTS Market Data API Overview What is Market Data? Key Features Types of Market Data Market Data Workflow Common Use Cases

EQ, SL, A). symbol Symbol 👁 Y Exchange defined trading code used to identify an instrument. expiryDate ExpiryDate 👁 Y ExpiryDate represents the date on which a derivative contract expires. optionType OptionType ↗ Y OptionType strikePrice StrikePrice 👁 Y The strike price is the predetermined price at which the buyer of a call option can exercise their rights to buy the underlying asset. DisplayName DisplayName 👁 A user-friendly name of the instrument used for display purposes in applications. Description Description 👁 A detailed description of the instrument, including company or contract details. Series Series 👁 The exchange defined series under which the instrument is listed (eg. EQ, SL, A). NameWithSeries NameWithSeries 👁 The instrument name appended with its series. InstrumentID InstrumentID 👁 A unique system-generated identifier assigned to the instrument by the exchange or trading system. PriceBand Object The permitted price range within which the instrument can trade during a session. High High 👁 The upper limit of the price band for the instrument. Low Low 👁 The lower limit of the price band for the instrument. CreditRating CreditRating 👁 The credit rating assigned to the instrument, if applicable. FreezeQty FreezeQty 👁 The maximum order quantity allowed per order for the instrument. TickSize TickSize 👁 The minimum price movement allowed for the instrument. LotSize LotSize 👁 The minimum tradable quantity for the instrument. UnderlyingInstrumentId UnderlyingInstrumentId 👁 The unique instrument identifier of the underlying asset for a derivative contract. UnderlyingIndexName UnderlyingIndexName 👁 The name of the underlying index on which the derivative contract is based. ContractExpiration ContractExpiration 👁 The date on which a derivative contract expires and is settled as per exchange rules. ContractExpirationString ContractExpirationString 👁 The contract expiration date represented as a formatted string.
